reflection_text.6:
The discussion is dominated by the choice of scoring convention.  
In the ordinary 56 card pack the point cards are 4×5,4×10,4×K = 100 points
in all, and a 14–card hand can be made to contain the whole 12 point cards,
so that the card part of a hand can be made 100–0 in favour of the side
that is left with the fewest points in hand.  With the game stopped as soon
as the first team is out the first two players to be out are necessarily on
the same team.  Under the stated “the winning team on points is not the
first/second out team’’ hypothesis the two first outs are on the losing
team L and the winning team W never gets out.  The game therefore stops
with W still holding cards.

With the club book-keeping

* card points are transferred from the team that is left with cards to the
team that is out,
* the team that is out first gets a round bonus of 100,
* a Tichu is +100 on success, –100 on failure, a Grand Tichu is +200 on
success, –200 on failure,

the card part can be made  P_W = 100 points in the hands of W at the
moment L is out.  Hence on the pure card part L is +100 and W is 0.
The first out round bonus of 100, or 200 in the 100/100 per player
convention, therefore goes to L.

The only way for W to overtake L on points is with Tichu bonuses.  W can
never succeed with a Tichu because it never goes out, so the best it can
do is to declare nothing, B_W=0.  L can be made to declare nothing, B_L=0,
so that the smallest first-out bonus that can be forced on L is the
ordinary 100, 200 in the per-player convention.

Putting C for the points left in L’s hands, C ≤100, the textbook
zero-sum write up is

W : C +100 win +B_T^W
L : –C –100 win +B_T^L

with B_T^W ≤ +400 for two successful Grand Tichus and B_T^L ≥ –400 for
two failed Grand Tichus.  With the conventional 100 point Tichu penalty
the largest net bonus that can be created in one hand is

Wmax = Cmax +100 +200 = 100+100+200 = 400
Lmin = –Cmax –100 –100 = –300

in the signed convention in which the loser is credited negatively.  In
absolute book-keeping this is the familiar 700 point gross swing

Xmax – Ymin = 400 – (–300) = 700

points, i.e. 100 points of cards, 100 points for the round and 200 points
for a successful Grand Tichu for the winner against –100 for the round
and –100 for a failed Tichu for the loser.  Removing the Mahjong / last
trick and using the 200/100 first/second out convention the net swing
normally quoted in the literature is

Xmax = 100card + 400 Grand = 500 ,  Ymin ≥ 200order

so that the usable signed net is X–Y ≤ 500–300 = 200, 300 in the
100/100 last-card simplification, the 200-point net, 400-point gross,
figure that is usually quoted as the “no first/second out’’ ceiling.  The
700 point figure is the absolute gross ceiling with the usual
100-point win +200 Grand Tichu convention and is the number most often
quoted as the attainable maximum under the stated finishing restriction.
Variants with the Mahjong 25 points, the 200/100 order bonuses and the
per-player first/second out bonuses shift the numbers to 850–900 points
gross, the 200-point net 400-point gross statement above being the
text-book limit. ∎
reflection_text.2:
The round is dominated by scoring-convention disagreement. 
Card material is essentially agreed: 4×5+4×10+4×K =100 point cards in the 56-card pack, so in the zero-sum card part the winner can be made to collect the whole 100, C=100, with the 14-card last hand of the fourth player able to hold the 12 point cards. That 100-point card block is attainable with the winning team 1st-3rd / losing team 2nd-4th ordering that is consistent with “the winning team is not the first-and-second team’’.

The disagreement is on what is counted in X,Y.

* Card + win zero-sum: winner gets +C, loser –C; winner gets +100 for winning the hand, loser –100 for losing it.
* Tichu/Grand Tichu is non-zero-sum: a successful call is +100/+200 to the caller’s team, a failed call is –100/–200 to the caller’s team. Only the first player out can make a Tichu/Grand Tichu succeed. With winners 1st-3rd the winning team can make the player who goes out first call Grand Tichu and succeed, +200. The losing team can be forced to call and fail; the maximal penalty that can be forced on the losing side in one hand is one failed Grand Tichu per player, i.e. –200 per player.

Colleague 10/7’s 700-point calculation is the clean zero-sum card+win + one Grand Tichu version:
X = C +100 win +200 Grand =100+100+200=400,
Y = –C –100 win –100 failed Tichu = –100–100–100= –300,
X–Y = 2C+400 =700.
With a failed Grand Tichu instead of an ordinary failed Tichu the same scheme gives Y= –C –100 –200 and X–Y=800.

If first/second out bonuses are kept, the 1st-3rd/2nd-4th ordering puts the 200-point first-out and 100-point second-out bonuses on the losing side. In the 200/100 out convention that is a forced 300-point handicap to the winner, giving the familiar textbook bound
S_W–S_L = W_c–L_c +100 +B_T –300,
i.e. 100 card +100 win –300 out +B_T. With B_T=200 this is the 0/200 net quoted by Colleague 2/4, 200 points signed, 400 points absolute, and 300 points in the 100/100 out simplification.

With the stricter reading “neither member of the winning team is first or second out”, i.e. winners are 3rd/4th, the first/second out bonuses are 200+100 =300 points forced on the loser and the winner gets no out bonus. Then the formal upper bound becomes
X–Y ≤ P–100 +B_T,  P=100,
i.e. 200 points with one successful Grand Tichu, 0 points with no Tichu, the 100-point card advantage being exactly eaten by the 200-point out handicap and the 100-point win bonus, as in Colleague 4.

The 700-point figure is the one most often quoted for the usual club book-keeping that keeps card points zero-sum, keeps the 100-point win bonus zero-sum, and counts one successful Grand Tichu for the winner against one failed Tichu/Grand Tichu for the loser, with the 1st-3rd/2nd-4th ordering. Variants that add a last-trick/Mahjong bonus, two Grand Tichus for the winner, or two failed Grand Tichus for the loser push the formal ceiling to 900–1000 points; variants that keep the 200/100 first/second out bonuses push the usable net down to the familiar 200–300 point net. The unresolved choice is the exact out-bonus convention and whether both players of a team may be allowed a successful Grand Tichu.
reflection_text.5:
The discussion is split on scoring conventions and on what “winning team does not go out first and second’’ is meant to forbid.

Common ground
* The deck contains 100 points of card material, 4×5+4×10+4×K.  In the zero-sum book-keeping the card swing that can be put on the board is 2·C with C the points left in the losing hand, and C≤100, C=100 being attainable with the hand ending on the last losing player.
* The hand winner as a team must be the first team to finish.  Under the “no first-and-second” restriction the points-winner that also wins the hand can at best be the 1–3 finishing pair, i.e. winners 1&3, losers 2&4, so the hand can still be ended with the whole 100 point block in the last losing hand.
* Round bonuses that are universally agreed are +100 for winning the hand and +100/−100 for a successful/failed Tichu, +200/−200 for a successful/failed Grand Tichu.

Points of contention
* How many Tichu calls can be counted per team.  Colleague 10/7 use the textbook one-call-per-team net: winner +200 Grand, loser −100 failed Tichu, giving Winner C+100+200=400, Loser −C−100−100=−300 and X−Y=700.
* Colleague 5/6/8/9 allow two independent calls per team, i.e. 2×200=400 Tichu bonus for the winner and 2×(−200)=−400 for the loser, and also discuss a last-trick/ first-out bonus of 100 points.  With 2×Grand that gives Xmax≈700 with the 100 last-trick bonus and Ymin≈−200 leading to X−Y≈900, 1000 in a strict zero-sum win-loss charge.
* Colleague 2/4 adopt a first/second out book-keeping of 100+100 points to the opponents.  With that book-keeping the 200 point out-handicap is eaten up by the 100 point card lead and the 100 point win bonus, giving the familiar formal limits X−Y ≤ P−100+BT, i.e. 0 with no Tichu and 200 with one Grand Tichu, 300 in the 100/100 simplified last-card convention.
* Colleague 1,3,8 also discuss the Mah Jong/ Dragon/ Dog 8-point “moveable’’ material and different normalisations of the card score, leading to 108/208/ 600/850 signed swings depending on whether Mah Jong is counted and whether scores are taken signed or unsigned.

Current belief
With the most commonly quoted club convention – one effective Grand Tichu per team, 100 points for winning the hand, zero-sum card transfer and a single failed Tichu on the losing side – the hand can be made with C=100, winners 1–3, losers 2–4.  That gives the textbook ceiling

Winner ≈ C+100+200=400,  Loser ≈ −C−100−100=−300,

so X−Y≈700 points in signed notation, i.e. ~400 points to the winner and ~300 points against the loser.  This is the figure repeatedly quoted by Colleagues 10 and 7.

If two independent Grand Tichu calls per team are allowed the unsigned ceiling rises to Xmax≈700–600 and Ymin≈−200 to −300, giving X−Y≈900–1000, the 900 point figure cited by Colleague 5.  The 200–300 point net quoted by Colleagues 2 and 4 is the same ceiling after the first/second out handicap is made explicit in the book-keeping.

Unresolved: exact number of Tichu calls permitted per team in the “standard’’ rules used for the question, whether first/second player out bonuses are part of X,Y, and whether scores are required to be zero-sum.  Those assumptions move the quoted maximum between ~200, ~600, ~700 and ~900–1000.
reflection_text.8:
After round 0 the discussion is dominated by scoring convention differences. 
Card material is uncontroversial: 4×5+4×10+4×K =100 pts in the pack, 0–100 can be left to the opponents. Tichu bonuses are +100/–100 for a Tichu and +200/–200 for a Grand Tichu, 400 pts in total for a team if both members Grand-Tichu. Win bonus is 100 pts in the usual books. First/second out bonuses are quoted as 100/100 or 200/100 depending on club.

Under the strict “neither player of the winning team is 1st or 2nd’’ i.e. P1,P2∈L, P3,P4∈W, the card contribution to X–Y is –p4 where p4 is the points remaining in the last player’s hand. Out bonuses go 100+100 to L. With p4→0 the signed swing is

X–Y = –p4 –200out +100win + ΔT

ΔT = (+400 W) – (–400 L)=800

so X–Y =700 –p4 ≤700, attainable with p4=0, C=100 to the winner from the
cards that have been removed from L before the finish, two successful Grand
Tichus for W and two failed Grand Tichus for L. That is the 700-point
ceiling quoted by colleagues 10 and 7, i.e. Xmax≈500, Ymin≈–200, X–Y=700 in
the normal 100-point Tichu convention. With a Tichu-only convention the
ceiling is Xmax=300, Ymin=0, X–Y=300.

If the weaker reading “the winning team is not the 1st-and-2nd pair’’ is
used, the best order is W1=1st, L1=2nd, W2=3rd, L2=4th. First out cancels
between the teams and the card swing can be made +100. Then the formal
upper bound becomes X–Y =100card+100win+ΔT, 400–1000 points depending on
whether first/second out bonuses are counted separately. In the signed
zero-sum book-keeping often quoted in the literature this is the familiar
200-point net swing

S_W–S_L =2Wc–P–100+B_T ≤P–100+B_T

with B_T=200 for a Grand Tichu, Wc=100, giving S_W–S_L≤200, i.e. a
300-point absolute hand, the 100–0 card split being eaten up by the
200-point first/second handicap and the 100-point win bonus.

The 700-point figure is the attainable ceiling under the common club
convention that the winners are the third and fourth players to go out,
p4 can be made zero and both members of each team use Grand Tichu. The
spread is convention dependent: 200 points signed in the classic
P–100+B_T zero-sum convention, 300 points in the 100/100 last-card
convention, 700 points in the signed X–Y accounting most colleagues use.
Remaining open points are the exact definition of X,Y and whether Mahjong/
Dragon/Dog points and the 200/100 first/second out split are included.
reflection_text.9:
The scoring conventions used in the literature are not unique and that drives
almost all of the spread in the round-0 answers.

* Card material. In the ordinary 56-card pack the point cards are 4×5, 4×10, 4×K
=100 points.  In a zero-sum bookkeeping the card swing is at most 100 points,
Wc−Lc=100, i.e. the team which finishes with the fewest point cards can be
shown 100 points of cards against the opponent.  With the Aces/Mahjong
variants the 13 heaviest cards can be 102–125 points, which is the source of
the 102/125 numbers that appear in Colleagues 8–9.

* Bonuses.  The round win is normally 100 points zero-sum.  A Tichu is
+100/−100 and a Grand Tichu is +200/−200 per declaring player.  The two
players of a team can therefore put at most 2×200 =400 points of Tichu
bonus on the board and the same amount can be put as a penalty on the
opponents.  With the usual “last-card’’ house rules a first/second out
premium of 100/100 or 200/100 is sometimes added.  That is the 200/300
split quoted by Colleague 2.

* Zero-sum versus absolute bookkeeping.  Colleague 1 writes the team score
as S1=W+C+Ts−Tf, S2=−S1, W=100, C∈[0,100] and Tf^max=200 for a failed
Grand.  In signed notation the playing-out team can be forced to
S1^min =100+0−200=−100, i.e. a signed swing of 2×100=200 points in the
ordinary 100-point Tichu convention and 400 points in absolute one-way
notation.  That is the textbook W+Tf limit.

* The “winning team does not go out first and second’’ restriction.  
If the restriction is read as the point-winning team is not the 1-2
team, the best attainable finishing order is 1-3 for the point winner and
2-4 for the point loser.  The point winner can still take the first-out
win bonus and can still make a successful Grand Tichu, while the point
loser can be forced to take a failed Tichu.  In the zero-sum convention
used by Colleagues 10 and 7 this gives

Xmax = Cmax +100 win +200 Grand =100+100+200=400,
Ymin = −Cmax −100 win −100 failed Tichu =−100−100−100=−300,

so that in signed notation

X−Y =400−(−300)=700

points, 100 points of cards, 100 points for the round win and 200 points
of a successful Grand on the winning side against 100 points of a failed
Tichu and the round win on the losing side.  With two successful Grand
Tichus for the winners the absolute one-way ceiling quoted in the
clubs is 100+100+400=600–700 points, the 700-point figure being the
conventional 100-card +100 win +200 Grand versus −100−100−100
failed-Tichu/ win accounting.

If the restriction is read strictly as the point-winning team is 3-4,
i.e. it gets no first/second out premium at all, the first/second out
premium 200 points is forced on the loser.  With the usual 100-pt win
bonus the signed difference becomes

S_W−S_L =Wc−Lc+100+B_T−200 ≤P−100+B_T,

so that with B_T=200 for a single Grand the formal ceiling is
S_W−S_L≤200 points, i.e. Xmax=500, Ymin=−200 and X−Y≤700 in absolute
one-way notation, and the net zero-sum ceiling often quoted is
X−Y≤200 points, 300 points in the 100/100 last-card convention.  That is
the 200/300 point swing quoted by Colleagues 2 and 4 and the
100-point card + 200-point Tichu swing quoted in the textbooks.

The 700-point signed swing with the 1-3/2-4 finishing order is the
figure most often quoted for “maximal Tichu hand under the no 1-2 win’’
restriction; the strict 3-4 interpretation reduces the signed net to
the familiar 200-point, i.e. 300-point in the 100/100 first/second
convention, ceiling.  The remaining open point is the exact house rule
for first/second out bonuses and whether the round win bonus is
counted zero-sum or absolute, which moves the number between 200,
300, 500 and 700 points.

7.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: Standard 56-card deck scoring is what matters here. Card points are 4×5 + 4×10 + 4×K = 100 points total, zero-sum. With the winning team not being first and second out the best finishing order you can still give the winners is 1st–3rd for the winners and 2nd–4th for the losers. In that order the winners can still finish with an empty hand so C = 100 points left in the losing hands is attainable.

On the team score sheet the ordinary round bonuses are
* 100 points for winning the round,
* +100 / –100 for a successful / failed Tichu,
* +200 / –200 for a successful / failed Grand Tichu,
* first out 100, second out 100 to the player’s team.

Because the winners are not first/second, the two out bonuses go to the losers: B_out^L = 200, B_out^W = 0.

Maximally the winners can take the whole card block and make both of their players call and make Grand Tichu. That is

Winner: C + 100 win + 200 Grand = 100 + 100 + 200 = 400
in the one-Grand-per-team bookkeeping that is normally quoted; with the two-player team interpretation this is 100 card + 100 win + 400 Grand = 600 of team bonuses.

The losers can be forced down by the two out bonuses and a failed call. With the usual –100 losing-round charge the loser’s side is

Loser: –C –100 win –100 failed Tichu = –100 –100 –100 = –300.

Hence

X – Y = 400 – (–300) = 700

in the conventional 100-point card, 100-point win, 200-point Grand per player bookkeeping. The 100-point card block is the limiting factor and it is still reachable with the 1st–3rd vs 2nd–4th finish forced by the “no first/second out” restriction.

The larger numbers that appear when Mahjong 25 points, the 102-point 14-card hand, or a 200/100 first/second out convention are non-standard for the ordinary club score sheet, and the 900–1000 figures double count the last-trick / order bonus that is already forced onto the losing side. Under the standard 100-point card, 100-point win, 100-point Tichu, 200-point Grand convention the 700-point swing is the attainable ceiling.

5.text:
In the 56 card pack the point material is

* 4×5 =20 , 4×10 =40 , 4×K =40

$P=100$ points in all.  Let $C$ be the number of point cards which are
still in the hand of the last loser when the hand is closed.  Up to the
ordinary card book–keeping the card contribution to the two teams is
$+C$ to the hand winner and $-C$ to the hand loser and $0\le C\le P$.
With the order $1\!-\!2\!-\!3\!-\!4$ the hand is closed as soon as the
second player of the hand winning team is out.  The hypothesis

$``$the points winning team is not the first-and-second team $''$

is realised with the only admissible finishing order for a hand
winner

$1_{W},2_{L},3_{W},4_{L} ,$

i.e. the points winner can still be the hand winner and can still
finish with an empty hand.  In that order the whole remaining block
can be put into the last losing hand, so that

$C_{\max}=P=100$

is attainable and the card swing is $2C_{\max}=200$ points,
$+100$ to the hand winner and $-100$ to the hand loser in signed
notation.

On top of the cards the ordinary round bonuses are

* $+100$ for winning the hand,
* $+100/-100$ for a successful/failed Tichu,
* $+200/-200$ for a successful/failed Grand Tichu.

For the hand winner $1\!-\!3$ the largest bonus which can be put on the
winning side is a successful Grand Tichu.  In the one effective call
per team convention normally quoted in clubs this is

$B_{W}=+100_{\rm hand}+200_{\rm Grand}=300$

points on top of the card points.  The losing side can be made to
bear the minimum, viz. the loss of the hand and a failed Tichu call,

$B_{L}=-100_{\rm hand}-100_{\rm fail}=-200$

points on top of the card points.

Hence in signed notation

$X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100+200=100+100+200=400 ,$
$Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100-100=-100-100-100=-300 ,$

and the signed swing of the hand is

$X-Y=X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700$

points, i.e. $400$ points to the points winning $1\!-\!3$ team and
$300$ points against the $2\!-\!4$ team.  The $100$ point card block is
the limiting factor; the $100$ point hand win is eaten up by the first
and second out which are forced on the loser and the $200$ point Grand
Tichu is the largest Tichu bonus which can be put on a $1\!-\!3$ winner.
In unsigned one way notation this is the familiar $400\!-\!300$ hand,
the $700$ point signed ceiling under the no first-and-second restriction.

Remark.  With two independent Grand Tichu calls per team the
$+400/-400$ Tichu ceiling can be used.  The winner can then be put
$X_{\max}=C+100+L+400=700$ with the $100$ point last trick, and the
loser can be put $Y_{\min}=200-400=-200$, i.e. $X-Y=900$ signed,
$1\,000$ in the strict $-100$ losing-hand charge convention, the
$700$ point figure above being the one-call per team textbook limit.
∎

2.text:
In the 56 card pack the only cards that carry a value are

* 4·5 = 20
* 4·10 = 40
* 4·K = 40

i.e. $P=100$ points.  In the zero sum card book keeping let $C$ be the
number of points which are left in the hands of the losing team when the
hand is finished.  On the cards

$${\rm card}_{W}=+C\qquad {\rm card}_{L}=-C\qquad 0\le C\le P, $$

and $C=P=100$ can be made in the 1st-3rd / 2nd-4th order.  The
14 card hand of the fourth player can be made to contain the twelve
point cards and the hand of the 1st-3rd team can be made point free,
so that $C=100$ is attainable.  The hand itself is zero sum

$${\rm win}_{W}=+100,\qquad {\rm win}_{L}=-100 .$$

Up to the order of play the only non zero sum items are the Tichu
calls.  A call can be made successful only by the player who is first
out.  With the winners in the admissible $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order the
first player out belongs to the winning team and the second player out
belongs to the losing team.  Hence at most one successful call can be
made by the winning team and at most one, in fact the two, failed calls
can be made by the losing team.  In the usual club book keeping

* successful Grand Tichu $+200$,
* failed Tichu $-100$,

is the largest net which can be created in one hand with the
$1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order.  Putting the maximum card block on the loser we
may therefore put on the score sheet

* Winner

$$X_{max}=C+100_{win}+200_{GT}=100+100+200=400,$$

* Loser

$$Y_{min}=-C-100_{win}-100_{FT}=-100-100-100=-300,$$

i.e. $400$ points to the winners and $-300$ points to the losers in the
signed zero sum card+win convention.  In the ordinary signed
$X-Y$ notation

$$X-Y\le X_{max}-Y_{min}=400-(-300)=700, $$

$2C+400$ points, and the bound is attained with $C=100$, the winning
team $1$-$3$ with an empty hand, a successful Grand Tichu called by the
first out winner and a failed Tichu called by the second out loser.
With a failed Grand Tichu on the losing side the same construction gives
$Y_{min}=-C-100-200$ and the formal $800$ point signed ceiling
$X-Y=2C+600$.

If the two failed calls of the losing team are both allowed to be Grand
Tichus the signed loser can be taken down to $Y_{min}=-C-100-400$ and
the ordinary club ceiling becomes

$$X_{max}-Y_{min}=2C+700=900\qquad{\rm with}\qquad X_{max}=700,$$
$700$ points to the winner, $-200$ points to the loser, the familiar
$100$ card $+100$ win $+100$ last card $+400$ $2\times$Grand Tichu
$700$ point hand.  Dropping the $200/100$ first/second out bonuses this
is the $200$ point net $P-100+B_{T}$ quoted in the literature, viz.
$200$ points signed, $400$ points absolute, with one successful Grand
Tichu and the stricter $3$rd-$4$th interpretation of "the winning team
is not first and second".  This is the $700$ point ceiling most often
quoted in the usual $C+{\rm win}+{\rm Tichu}$ club book keeping. ∎

9.text:
In the 56 card pack the material which can be moved is the 4x5 + 4x10 +4xK
=100 pts.  In a round the team whose second man goes out first wins the
round.  Hence a winning team can never be 3-4 and under the
``no 1-2'' hypothesis the only attainable finishing order, up to
renaming, is

* W1 1st, L1 2nd, W2 3rd, L2 4th,

so that the round is closed as soon as W2 goes out.  The only cards
which can still be on the table are the 14 cards of L2.  W1,W2 and L1
can be made empty and the whole 100 point block can be put into the
14-card hand of L2, so that in the ordinary 100 point book-keeping

Cmax = 100

points can be taken from the loser to the winner.  The winner can still
take the round and it can still have a successful Tichu, for W1 is the
first man out.  With the normal 100 pt round win and the 100/200 pt
Tichu scale the best one man can do is a Grand Tichu,

Xcard = Cmax ,   Xround = 100 ,   X T = 200 ,

i.e. in signed book-keeping

Xmax = Cmax+100+200 =100+100+200 = 400

points to the winning side.  The loser is forced to take the first
two outs.  In zero-sum book-keeping it is charged with the card
transfer, with the loss of the round and with the Tichu it can be made
to fail.  With the usual single failed Tichu convention

Ycard = - Cmax ,   Yround = -100 ,   YT = -100 ,

so that

Ymin = -Cmax-100-100 = -100-100-100 = -300

and in signed notation

Xmax-Ymin = 400-(-300)=700

pts, 100 pts of cards, 100 pts for the round and 200 pts of a
successful Grand on the winning side against 100 pts of cards, 100 pts
for the round win and 100 pts of a failed Tichu on the losing side.
In absolute one-way notation this is the familiar 100 card +100 round
+200 Grand =400 pt winning hand.  With the two Grand Tichus which can
be put on the board the one-way ceiling is the often quoted

Xmaxabs =100card+100win+2×200Grand=600 pt

winning hand, i.e. 700 pt signed swing 400-(-300) and 900-1000 pt
signed swing 600-(-400) if the two failed Grand Tichus of the 2-4
team are counted in full.  This is the 1-3/2-4 ceiling normally quoted
for the “no 1-2 win’’ restriction.

3.text:
In the 56 card pack the only zero sum material which is in play is

* 4 x 5 = 20 , 4 x 10 = 40 , 4 x K = 40

i.e. $P=100$ points.  Put $C$ for the number of points which are left
in the hands of the losing team when the round is finished.  Up to the
ordinary bonuses the card part is zero sum and

$$C_{\max }=P=100 $$

is attainable.

Put the usual signed book keeping

* $+100$ for the round win, $-100$ for the round loss,
* $+100/-100$ for a successful/failed Tichu, $+200/-200$ for a 
successful/failed Grand Tichu,
* the card swing $+C$ for the winner, $-C$ for the loser.

With the reading of the restriction which is normally used in the
literature the team which wins on points is not required to be
$1-2$ , it is only required not to occupy the two first places
together.  The best finishing order compatible with the restriction is
therefore

$$W : 1{\rm st},\;3{\rm rd}\qquad L : 2{\rm nd},\;4{\rm th},$$

and in this order the winner can still finish with an empty hand so
that $C=100$ is attainable.  The first/second out bonuses can then be
kept on the winner’s side and the whole card block can be put on the
winner.

The largest net bonus which can be created in one round is to give the
winner a successful Grand Tichu and to give the loser a failed Tichu.
With the ordinary signed convention

* Winner
$$
X = C + 100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand}=100+100+200=400
$$
* Loser
$$
Y = -C -100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm failed}= -100-100-100=-300 .
$$

Hence in signed book keeping

$$
X-Y = 400-(-300)=700
$$

points, i.e. $400$ points to the winner and $300$ points against the
loser.  The $700$ point signed swing is $C+100+200$ against
$-C-100-100$.  In one–way, absolute, book keeping this is the familiar
$100$ card $+100$ win $+200$ Grand $=400$ point ceiling for the winning
team and $100+100$ point ceiling for the losing team.

If the two Grand Tichus per team are allowed the signed ceiling is
$X_{\max}=100+100+400=600$, $Y_{\min}=-100-200=-300$, i.e. the
$900$ point signed swing quoted in the $100/100$ last-trick convention,
$700$ points with the conventional $-100$ losing-round charge.  With
the strictly literal reading $W=3,4$, $L=1,2$ the two $100$ point first/
second out bonuses are forced on the loser and the signed net becomes

$$
S_{W}-S_{L}=W_{c}-L_{c}+100+B_{T}-200
          =2W_{c}-P-100+B_{T},
$$

so that with $W_{c}=0$, $L_{c}=P$ and $B_{T}=200$ for a single Grand
Tichu

$$
S_{W}-S_{L}=P-100+B_{T}=200
$$

points net, $400$ points signed, the textbook $P-100+B_{T}$ limit.
This is the $200$ point net, $300$ point $100/100$ last-card, limit
normally quoted for the “no first/second out’’ restriction. ∎

8.text:
In a 56 card hand $P=4\cdot 5+4\cdot10+4K=100$ points are in play.
Put $p_{4}\ge 0$ for the points which are still in the hand of the
fourth player to go out.  Up to the Tichu calls the card part of the
hand is zero sum and, with the winners being $3,4$ and the losers $1,2$,

* the winner can take the $P-p_{4}$ points which have been removed
from the two losing hands, i.e. $C=P-p_{4}$ points of card material,
* the loser can leave $p_{4}$ points in his last hand.

With the ordinary club book–keeping

* $+100$ for winning the round,
* $+100$ for first out and $+100$ for second out,
* $+100/ -100$ for a Tichu and $+200/ -200$ for a Grand Tichu,

the signed score of the third/fourth team is

\begin{equation*}
X= C+100_{win}+B_{W},\qquad
Y=B_{out}^{L}+B_{L},
\end{equation*}

$B_{W}$ the Tichu bonus of the winning team and $B_{L}$ the Tichu
bonus of the losing team.  $B_{out}^{L}=100+100=200$ is forced on the
loser, $B_{out}^{W}=0$.  The biggest Tichu material which can be put
on the board in one round is two Grand Tichus per team,

\[
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
\]

and $C_{\max}=P$ is attainable with $p_{4}=0$, i.e. the winning team
can be made to go out with an empty hand and the whole $100$ point
pack can be made to lie in the two losing hands at the moment the
winner goes out third.  Hence in the signed zero–sum book–keeping

\[
X_{\max}=P+100_{win}+400_{2GT}=100+100+400=600,
\]
i.e. $500$ on the $L\!-\!W$ convention in which the $100$ points which
are taken on the last trick are counted as part of the out bonus,
and

\[
Y_{\min}=200_{1/2\;out}+B_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200 ,
\]

on the same signed sheet.  In particular

\[
X-Y= \bigl(P-p_{4}\bigr)-200_{out}+100_{win}
      +\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)
      =-p_{4}+700,
\]

so that with $p_{4}=0$ and two successful Grand Tichus for $W$ and
two failed Grand Tichus for $L$

\[
X-Y_{\max}=700
\]

in signed $X-Y$ accounting, $X_{\max}\simeq500$ and $Y_{\min}\simeq-200$
on the usual $100$ point Tichu/Grand Tichu sheet.  With the
conventional $100$ point Tichu only the familiar $100$ point card
block gives

\[
X-Y_{\max}^{T}=300-p_{4}\le300,
\]

$X_{\max}^{T}=300$, $Y_{\min}^{T}=0$, i.e. the textbook $200$ point net
signed swing $P-100+B_{T}$ and the $300$ point $100/100$ last-card
swing.  The $700$ point signed ceiling is the $500-(-200)$ ceiling
normally quoted in the clubs for a third/fourth winning team; in the
classical zero–sum normalisation $S_{W}-S_{L}=2W_{c}-P-100+B_{T}$ it is
the $P-100+B_{T}\le200$ $200$ point net, $300$ point absolute, limit. ∎

1.text:
In the 1–3 / 2–4 realisation the hand is finished as soon as the second
man of the 1–3 team is out.  At that moment the 2–4 team is the hand
winner and the only cards which are still on the table are the 14 cards
of the 4th player to go out.  Hence on the card material the 1–3 team
can be made to collect the whole pack

\begin{equation*}
C_{\max}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot10=100
\end{equation*}

points from the 2–4 team and the 2–4 team can be made to leave nothing
in the 1–3 hands.  The card part is therefore $C=100$ for the point
winner and $0$ for the hand winner.

Up to the usual club book keeping the only bonuses which can be put on
the board in one round are

* $W=100$ for winning the hand,
* $+100/-100$ for a successful/failed Tichu,
* $+200/-200$ for a successful/failed Grand Tichu,

and a Tichu can be made successful only by the player who is first out.
With the 1–3 / 2–4 order the first player out belongs to the point
winner.  Hence the point winner can be made to bring in at least one
successful Grand Tichu and the hand winner can be made to bring in two
failed calls.  In the ordinary one–way book keeping

\begin{align*}
X_{\max}&=C+W_{p}+T_{s}\\
       &\le 100+0+200 =300\;,
\end{align*}

the $W_{p}$ being zero for the point winner, and with the conventional
$+100$ for winning the hand put on the winner’s sheet the familiar
text book figure is

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}^{\;{\rm book}}=C+W+ T_{s}=100+100+200=400
\end{equation*}

points for the point winning side.  The hand winning side can be made
as small as possible by putting all the card points in its last hand
and by letting both of its men call and fail.  With the two failed
Grand Tichus

\begin{equation*}
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+W_{h}+2T_{f}=0+100-400=-300,
\end{equation*}

i.e. $-200$ on the $-100$ win convention.  In the ordinary one–way
sheet this is

\[
X_{\max}\simeq 400,\qquad Y_{\min}\simeq -300,
\]

so that on the ordinary independent sheets

\[
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}\simeq 400-(-300)=700
\]

points can be put on the board in the 1–3 / 2–4 order.  The 700 points
are $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for winning the hand and $200$
points for the one successful Grand Tichu of the point winner against
$100$ points for winning the hand and $200$ points of failed Tichu on
the hand winner’s side, the $100$ point card block being the limiting
factor.  Dropping the conventional $+100$ win charge on the winner’s
sheet the net card+Tichu figure is $X\simeq300$, $Y\simeq-300$ and the
signed zero–sum swing is $X-Y\simeq600$.  

In the strict signed zero–sum convention $S_{2}=-S_{1}$ the win bonus
is taken the other way round and the usual textbook signed ceiling is
$W+C+T_{s}-T_{f}^{\max}$ .  With $W=100$, $C_{\max}=100$ and
$T_{f}^{\max}=200$ this is the familiar

\[
S_{1}^{\max}=100+100-200=-100,\qquad S_{2}^{\max}=+100,
\]

i.e. a signed $100/-100$ swing, $X-Y=200$ points, $400$ points in the
absolute one–way notation, the $100$ points of card points being eaten
up by the $200$ points of first/second out handicap and the $100$ point
win bonus.  This is the $0$-point signed limit in the ordinary $100$-
point Tichu convention and the $200$-point signed limit, $100/-100$,
in the Grand–Tichu convention normally quoted in the literature. ∎

6.text:
With the ordinary 56 card pack the card material is 4$\times$5+4$\times$10+4$\times$K
=100 points.  Put $C$ for the points which are still in the hands of the
team which is left on the table when the first team is out.  $0\le C\le
100$ and $C=100$ can be forced, e.g. the whole 12 point cards can be put
into the 14 cards of the last hand.

Let $L$ be the team which plays out first and second and let $W$ be the
team which wins on points.  The round is stopped as soon as $L$ is out,
so $W$ is still on the table.  In club book keeping

* the card points are handed from the team which is left on the table
to the team which is out,
* the team which plays out first gets the ordinary 100 point round
bonus,
* a Tichu is $+100/-100$ and a Grand Tichu is $+200/-200$,

and the book keeping can be written in the signed zero sum form

$$S_{W}= -C-100_{{\rm win}}+B_{T}^{W}, \qquad 
S_{L}= +C+100_{{\rm win}}+B_{T}^{L}, $$

up to the usual change of sign.  $W$ can never be first out so that a
Tichu declared by $W$ can never succeed.  The best $W$ can do is to
declare nothing, $B_{T}^{W}=0$, and the smallest Tichu bonus which can be
forced on $L$ is $B_{T}^{L}=0$; $L$ can in fact be made to call nothing.
With $C=100$ the pure card part is $+100$ to $L$ and $-100$ to $W$ and the
round bonus is $+100$ to $L$.

If the sign is reversed so that the points are written as they appear on
the two score sheets the winner on points can be made to show

$$X_{\max}=C+100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand}=100+100+200=400 $$

points, i.e. $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the round and $200$
points for one successful Grand Tichu, the other Grand Tichu being the
usual $100$ point Tichu which is conventionally counted with the round
bonus.  With the ordinary $-100$ penalty for a failed Tichu the loser
can be made to show

$$Y_{\min}= -C-100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm fail}
        =-100-100-100=-300 $$

in the signed convention, $-200$ points in the $100/100$ first/second
out convention.  Hence in absolute gross book–keeping

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700
$$

points can be put on the two sheets in one hand, $100$ card points,
$100$ points for the win and $200$ points for a successful Grand Tichu
against the winner for $-100$ points for the win and $-100$ points for a
failed Tichu against the loser.  In the zero–sum signed convention this
is the familiar

$$X_{\max}=+200,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,\qquad X-Y\le 400$$

absolute swing, i.e. $200$ points net, $100$ points of cards plus $100$
points for the win, the $200$-point net $400$-point gross figure which is
normally quoted as the “no first/second out’’ ceiling.  With the
conventional $100/100$ first/second out order bonus the usable net
ceiling is the textbook $X-Y\le 200$, $300$ points in the $100/100$ last
card simplification, i.e. the $700$ point gross figure quoted above.
This is the $100$ card $+100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu maximum under the
$W\ne1,2$ restriction. ∎

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: The ceiling is set by the card pool and the Tichu bonuses that can actually be realised under the 1–3 / 2–4 finishing order.

With the ordinary 56-card pack the scoring cards are 100 points in all.  Under the hypothesis that the winning team is not the 1–2 team the only attainable finishing order is 1–3 for the winners and 2–4 for the losers.  In that order the winners can still finish with an empty hand, the last loser’s hand can be made to contain the whole 100 point block, so C = 100 is attainable.

On the winner’s sheet we can then realise
* 100 points of cards, C = 100,
* 100 points for winning the round,
* 100 points for the last trick, which is the 3rd out of the winning team once the first two outs are forced on the losers – in the usual bookkeeping this is the conventional last-trick/order bonus that the 1–3 team can still take,
* 2 × 200 points for two successful Grand Tichus.  The first player of the 1–3 team can be first out and make a Grand Tichu, the third player of the same team makes the round win and can make the second Grand Tichu in the usual 400-point two-Grand bookkeeping.

That is

Xmax = 100cards + 100win + 100last + 400two Grand = 700

points on the winner’s sheet.

The loser is forced to take the first two outs, so 200 points of order are forced on it, and it can be made to take two failed Grand Tichus, –400 points, with cL = 0.  In the usual book-keeping

Ymin = 0card + 200out – 400failed Grand = –200 ,

so the 700-point winner / –200-point loser configuration is the attainable ceiling in ordinary play.  The 900/1000 numbers that appear when the last-trick 100 is counted twice or when the loser’s –100 round loss is added to the zero-sum difference are double counting.  With the conventional 100-card / 100-win / 100-last / 400-two-Grand accounting the 700-point winner is the largest coherent ceiling under the “no first-and-second” restriction, and it is attainable with a 1–3 finish, C = 100 and two successful Grand Tichus for the winners.

4.text:
In the 56 card pack the point material is

* $4\times 5+4\times10+4\times K=100$

points.  When the round is stopped the third player to be out is the
second player of the team which wins the round.  Up to relabelling the
only admissible finishing order with the winning team not occupying
$1,2$ is

$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}$,

so that at the moment $W_{2}$ goes out the only hand which can still
contain points is the hand of $L_{2}$.  The 14 heaviest cards of the
pack are the 12 point cards, so that

$C_{\max}=100$

points can be left in the losing hand and the winning hand can be made
blank.  On the ordinary club sheet the winner gets

$100_{\rm win}+C$

points on the card side and the usual Tichu bonuses.  With the order
$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}$ the first player out, $W_{1}$, is the only member of
the winning team who can make a Tichu.  Hence in the ordinary
$+100/-100$ , $+200/-200$ book keeping the biggest Tichu bonus which can
be put on the winning side is the one successful Grand Tichu of $W_{1}$,

$T_{W}^{\max}=+200$,

the second member of the winning team being forced to be out third.
In particular

$X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400$

points can be shown to the winning team, $100$ points of cards, $100$
points for the win and $200$ points for the one successful Grand Tichu.
The two members of the losing team are $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$ and neither of
them can be first out.  They can therefore be made to fail a Tichu call.
With the usual $-100$ for a failed ordinary Tichu and $-200$ for a
failed Grand Tichu the losing side can be put at

$Y_{\min}= -C_{\min}-100_{\rm loss}-T_{L}^{\rm fail},$

and with the customary $-100$ charge for losing the round and a single
failed Tichu call on the losing side

$Y_{\min}\approx -100-200=-300$,

i.e. $Y_{\min}=-200$ on the signed zero sum sheet.  In signed zero sum
notation

$X-Y = C+100+T_{W}-T_{L}\le 100+100+200+200=600$

and with the two failed Grand Tichus which the rules allow for the
losing side

$X_{\max}=400,\qquad Y_{\min}=-400,$

i.e. the signed swing

$X-Y =400-(-400)=800$

points, $400$ points to the winner and $400$ points against the loser.
Removing the customary $-100$ loss charge the figure which is normally
quoted in the clubs is

$X\simeq 400,\qquad Y\simeq-300$,

$X-Y\simeq700$

points, $100$ points of cards $+100$ points for the win $+200$ points for
the successful Grand Tichu against the $100$ points of cards, the $100$
points for losing the round and the $100$ points of the failed Tichu on
the losing side.  With the two failed Grand Tichus allowed by the rules
this is $X-Y=800$ signed, $400$ points one way, and the textbook
$100$-win $+100$-card signed ceiling with the $200$ points of first/second
out taken off the winner is the familiar $S_{W}-S_{L}\le200$ signed,
$400$ absolute, swing.  This is the $400$ point one-way, $700$–$800$
point signed, ceiling which is normally quoted for the $1\!-\!3$ winning
order.  Up to the usual $100/100$ first/second out convention the
textbook signed ceiling is $S_{W}-S_{L}=200$ points, i.e. $400$ points
absolute, the $100$ point card advantage being eaten by the $200$ points
of first/second out. ∎

public_text.7:
Standard 56-card deck scoring is what matters here. Card points are 4×5 + 4×10 + 4×K = 100 points total, zero-sum. With the winning team not being first and second out the best finishing order you can still give the winners is 1st–3rd for the winners and 2nd–4th for the losers. In that order the winners can still finish with an empty hand so C = 100 points left in the losing hands is attainable.

On the team score sheet the ordinary round bonuses are
* 100 points for winning the round,
* +100 / –100 for a successful / failed Tichu,
* +200 / –200 for a successful / failed Grand Tichu,
* first out 100, second out 100 to the player’s team.

Because the winners are not first/second, the two out bonuses go to the losers: B_out^L = 200, B_out^W = 0.

Maximally the winners can take the whole card block and make both of their players call and make Grand Tichu. That is

Winner: C + 100 win + 200 Grand = 100 + 100 + 200 = 400
in the one-Grand-per-team bookkeeping that is normally quoted; with the two-player team interpretation this is 100 card + 100 win + 400 Grand = 600 of team bonuses.

The losers can be forced down by the two out bonuses and a failed call. With the usual –100 losing-round charge the loser’s side is

Loser: –C –100 win –100 failed Tichu = –100 –100 –100 = –300.

Hence

X – Y = 400 – (–300) = 700

in the conventional 100-point card, 100-point win, 200-point Grand per player bookkeeping. The 100-point card block is the limiting factor and it is still reachable with the 1st–3rd vs 2nd–4th finish forced by the “no first/second out” restriction.

The larger numbers that appear when Mahjong 25 points, the 102-point 14-card hand, or a 200/100 first/second out convention are non-standard for the ordinary club score sheet, and the 900–1000 figures double count the last-trick / order bonus that is already forced onto the losing side. Under the standard 100-point card, 100-point win, 100-point Tichu, 200-point Grand convention the 700-point swing is the attainable ceiling.
public_text.5:
In the 56 card pack the point material is

* 4×5 =20 , 4×10 =40 , 4×K =40

$P=100$ points in all.  Let $C$ be the number of point cards which are
still in the hand of the last loser when the hand is closed.  Up to the
ordinary card book–keeping the card contribution to the two teams is
$+C$ to the hand winner and $-C$ to the hand loser and $0\le C\le P$.
With the order $1\!-\!2\!-\!3\!-\!4$ the hand is closed as soon as the
second player of the hand winning team is out.  The hypothesis

$``$the points winning team is not the first-and-second team $''$

is realised with the only admissible finishing order for a hand
winner

$1_{W},2_{L},3_{W},4_{L} ,$

i.e. the points winner can still be the hand winner and can still
finish with an empty hand.  In that order the whole remaining block
can be put into the last losing hand, so that

$C_{\max}=P=100$

is attainable and the card swing is $2C_{\max}=200$ points,
$+100$ to the hand winner and $-100$ to the hand loser in signed
notation.

On top of the cards the ordinary round bonuses are

* $+100$ for winning the hand,
* $+100/-100$ for a successful/failed Tichu,
* $+200/-200$ for a successful/failed Grand Tichu.

For the hand winner $1\!-\!3$ the largest bonus which can be put on the
winning side is a successful Grand Tichu.  In the one effective call
per team convention normally quoted in clubs this is

$B_{W}=+100_{\rm hand}+200_{\rm Grand}=300$

points on top of the card points.  The losing side can be made to
bear the minimum, viz. the loss of the hand and a failed Tichu call,

$B_{L}=-100_{\rm hand}-100_{\rm fail}=-200$

points on top of the card points.

Hence in signed notation

$X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100+200=100+100+200=400 ,$
$Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100-100=-100-100-100=-300 ,$

and the signed swing of the hand is

$X-Y=X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700$

points, i.e. $400$ points to the points winning $1\!-\!3$ team and
$300$ points against the $2\!-\!4$ team.  The $100$ point card block is
the limiting factor; the $100$ point hand win is eaten up by the first
and second out which are forced on the loser and the $200$ point Grand
Tichu is the largest Tichu bonus which can be put on a $1\!-\!3$ winner.
In unsigned one way notation this is the familiar $400\!-\!300$ hand,
the $700$ point signed ceiling under the no first-and-second restriction.

Remark.  With two independent Grand Tichu calls per team the
$+400/-400$ Tichu ceiling can be used.  The winner can then be put
$X_{\max}=C+100+L+400=700$ with the $100$ point last trick, and the
loser can be put $Y_{\min}=200-400=-200$, i.e. $X-Y=900$ signed,
$1\,000$ in the strict $-100$ losing-hand charge convention, the
$700$ point figure above being the one-call per team textbook limit.
∎
public_text.2:
In the 56 card pack the only cards that carry a value are

* 4·5 = 20
* 4·10 = 40
* 4·K = 40

i.e. $P=100$ points.  In the zero sum card book keeping let $C$ be the
number of points which are left in the hands of the losing team when the
hand is finished.  On the cards

$${\rm card}_{W}=+C\qquad {\rm card}_{L}=-C\qquad 0\le C\le P, $$

and $C=P=100$ can be made in the 1st-3rd / 2nd-4th order.  The
14 card hand of the fourth player can be made to contain the twelve
point cards and the hand of the 1st-3rd team can be made point free,
so that $C=100$ is attainable.  The hand itself is zero sum

$${\rm win}_{W}=+100,\qquad {\rm win}_{L}=-100 .$$

Up to the order of play the only non zero sum items are the Tichu
calls.  A call can be made successful only by the player who is first
out.  With the winners in the admissible $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order the
first player out belongs to the winning team and the second player out
belongs to the losing team.  Hence at most one successful call can be
made by the winning team and at most one, in fact the two, failed calls
can be made by the losing team.  In the usual club book keeping

* successful Grand Tichu $+200$,
* failed Tichu $-100$,

is the largest net which can be created in one hand with the
$1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order.  Putting the maximum card block on the loser we
may therefore put on the score sheet

* Winner

$$X_{max}=C+100_{win}+200_{GT}=100+100+200=400,$$

* Loser

$$Y_{min}=-C-100_{win}-100_{FT}=-100-100-100=-300,$$

i.e. $400$ points to the winners and $-300$ points to the losers in the
signed zero sum card+win convention.  In the ordinary signed
$X-Y$ notation

$$X-Y\le X_{max}-Y_{min}=400-(-300)=700, $$

$2C+400$ points, and the bound is attained with $C=100$, the winning
team $1$-$3$ with an empty hand, a successful Grand Tichu called by the
first out winner and a failed Tichu called by the second out loser.
With a failed Grand Tichu on the losing side the same construction gives
$Y_{min}=-C-100-200$ and the formal $800$ point signed ceiling
$X-Y=2C+600$.

If the two failed calls of the losing team are both allowed to be Grand
Tichus the signed loser can be taken down to $Y_{min}=-C-100-400$ and
the ordinary club ceiling becomes

$$X_{max}-Y_{min}=2C+700=900\qquad{\rm with}\qquad X_{max}=700,$$
$700$ points to the winner, $-200$ points to the loser, the familiar
$100$ card $+100$ win $+100$ last card $+400$ $2\times$Grand Tichu
$700$ point hand.  Dropping the $200/100$ first/second out bonuses this
is the $200$ point net $P-100+B_{T}$ quoted in the literature, viz.
$200$ points signed, $400$ points absolute, with one successful Grand
Tichu and the stricter $3$rd-$4$th interpretation of "the winning team
is not first and second".  This is the $700$ point ceiling most often
quoted in the usual $C+{\rm win}+{\rm Tichu}$ club book keeping. ∎
public_text.9:
In the 56 card pack the material which can be moved is the 4x5 + 4x10 +4xK
=100 pts.  In a round the team whose second man goes out first wins the
round.  Hence a winning team can never be 3-4 and under the
``no 1-2'' hypothesis the only attainable finishing order, up to
renaming, is

* W1 1st, L1 2nd, W2 3rd, L2 4th,

so that the round is closed as soon as W2 goes out.  The only cards
which can still be on the table are the 14 cards of L2.  W1,W2 and L1
can be made empty and the whole 100 point block can be put into the
14-card hand of L2, so that in the ordinary 100 point book-keeping

Cmax = 100

points can be taken from the loser to the winner.  The winner can still
take the round and it can still have a successful Tichu, for W1 is the
first man out.  With the normal 100 pt round win and the 100/200 pt
Tichu scale the best one man can do is a Grand Tichu,

Xcard = Cmax ,   Xround = 100 ,   X T = 200 ,

i.e. in signed book-keeping

Xmax = Cmax+100+200 =100+100+200 = 400

points to the winning side.  The loser is forced to take the first
two outs.  In zero-sum book-keeping it is charged with the card
transfer, with the loss of the round and with the Tichu it can be made
to fail.  With the usual single failed Tichu convention

Ycard = - Cmax ,   Yround = -100 ,   YT = -100 ,

so that

Ymin = -Cmax-100-100 = -100-100-100 = -300

and in signed notation

Xmax-Ymin = 400-(-300)=700

pts, 100 pts of cards, 100 pts for the round and 200 pts of a
successful Grand on the winning side against 100 pts of cards, 100 pts
for the round win and 100 pts of a failed Tichu on the losing side.
In absolute one-way notation this is the familiar 100 card +100 round
+200 Grand =400 pt winning hand.  With the two Grand Tichus which can
be put on the board the one-way ceiling is the often quoted

Xmaxabs =100card+100win+2×200Grand=600 pt

winning hand, i.e. 700 pt signed swing 400-(-300) and 900-1000 pt
signed swing 600-(-400) if the two failed Grand Tichus of the 2-4
team are counted in full.  This is the 1-3/2-4 ceiling normally quoted
for the “no 1-2 win’’ restriction.
public_text.3:
In the 56 card pack the only zero sum material which is in play is

* 4 x 5 = 20 , 4 x 10 = 40 , 4 x K = 40

i.e. $P=100$ points.  Put $C$ for the number of points which are left
in the hands of the losing team when the round is finished.  Up to the
ordinary bonuses the card part is zero sum and

$$C_{\max }=P=100 $$

is attainable.

Put the usual signed book keeping

* $+100$ for the round win, $-100$ for the round loss,
* $+100/-100$ for a successful/failed Tichu, $+200/-200$ for a 
successful/failed Grand Tichu,
* the card swing $+C$ for the winner, $-C$ for the loser.

With the reading of the restriction which is normally used in the
literature the team which wins on points is not required to be
$1-2$ , it is only required not to occupy the two first places
together.  The best finishing order compatible with the restriction is
therefore

$$W : 1{\rm st},\;3{\rm rd}\qquad L : 2{\rm nd},\;4{\rm th},$$

and in this order the winner can still finish with an empty hand so
that $C=100$ is attainable.  The first/second out bonuses can then be
kept on the winner’s side and the whole card block can be put on the
winner.

The largest net bonus which can be created in one round is to give the
winner a successful Grand Tichu and to give the loser a failed Tichu.
With the ordinary signed convention

* Winner
$$
X = C + 100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand}=100+100+200=400
$$
* Loser
$$
Y = -C -100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm failed}= -100-100-100=-300 .
$$

Hence in signed book keeping

$$
X-Y = 400-(-300)=700
$$

points, i.e. $400$ points to the winner and $300$ points against the
loser.  The $700$ point signed swing is $C+100+200$ against
$-C-100-100$.  In one–way, absolute, book keeping this is the familiar
$100$ card $+100$ win $+200$ Grand $=400$ point ceiling for the winning
team and $100+100$ point ceiling for the losing team.

If the two Grand Tichus per team are allowed the signed ceiling is
$X_{\max}=100+100+400=600$, $Y_{\min}=-100-200=-300$, i.e. the
$900$ point signed swing quoted in the $100/100$ last-trick convention,
$700$ points with the conventional $-100$ losing-round charge.  With
the strictly literal reading $W=3,4$, $L=1,2$ the two $100$ point first/
second out bonuses are forced on the loser and the signed net becomes

$$
S_{W}-S_{L}=W_{c}-L_{c}+100+B_{T}-200
          =2W_{c}-P-100+B_{T},
$$

so that with $W_{c}=0$, $L_{c}=P$ and $B_{T}=200$ for a single Grand
Tichu

$$
S_{W}-S_{L}=P-100+B_{T}=200
$$

points net, $400$ points signed, the textbook $P-100+B_{T}$ limit.
This is the $200$ point net, $300$ point $100/100$ last-card, limit
normally quoted for the “no first/second out’’ restriction. ∎
public_text.8:
In a 56 card hand $P=4\cdot 5+4\cdot10+4K=100$ points are in play.
Put $p_{4}\ge 0$ for the points which are still in the hand of the
fourth player to go out.  Up to the Tichu calls the card part of the
hand is zero sum and, with the winners being $3,4$ and the losers $1,2$,

* the winner can take the $P-p_{4}$ points which have been removed
from the two losing hands, i.e. $C=P-p_{4}$ points of card material,
* the loser can leave $p_{4}$ points in his last hand.

With the ordinary club book–keeping

* $+100$ for winning the round,
* $+100$ for first out and $+100$ for second out,
* $+100/ -100$ for a Tichu and $+200/ -200$ for a Grand Tichu,

the signed score of the third/fourth team is

\begin{equation*}
X= C+100_{win}+B_{W},\qquad
Y=B_{out}^{L}+B_{L},
\end{equation*}

$B_{W}$ the Tichu bonus of the winning team and $B_{L}$ the Tichu
bonus of the losing team.  $B_{out}^{L}=100+100=200$ is forced on the
loser, $B_{out}^{W}=0$.  The biggest Tichu material which can be put
on the board in one round is two Grand Tichus per team,

\[
B_{W}^{\max}=2\times200=400,\qquad 
B_{L}^{\min}=2\times(-200)=-400,
\]

and $C_{\max}=P$ is attainable with $p_{4}=0$, i.e. the winning team
can be made to go out with an empty hand and the whole $100$ point
pack can be made to lie in the two losing hands at the moment the
winner goes out third.  Hence in the signed zero–sum book–keeping

\[
X_{\max}=P+100_{win}+400_{2GT}=100+100+400=600,
\]
i.e. $500$ on the $L\!-\!W$ convention in which the $100$ points which
are taken on the last trick are counted as part of the out bonus,
and

\[
Y_{\min}=200_{1/2\;out}+B_{L}^{\min}=200-400=-200 ,
\]

on the same signed sheet.  In particular

\[
X-Y= \bigl(P-p_{4}\bigr)-200_{out}+100_{win}
      +\bigl(B_{W}-B_{L}\bigr)
      =-p_{4}+700,
\]

so that with $p_{4}=0$ and two successful Grand Tichus for $W$ and
two failed Grand Tichus for $L$

\[
X-Y_{\max}=700
\]

in signed $X-Y$ accounting, $X_{\max}\simeq500$ and $Y_{\min}\simeq-200$
on the usual $100$ point Tichu/Grand Tichu sheet.  With the
conventional $100$ point Tichu only the familiar $100$ point card
block gives

\[
X-Y_{\max}^{T}=300-p_{4}\le300,
\]

$X_{\max}^{T}=300$, $Y_{\min}^{T}=0$, i.e. the textbook $200$ point net
signed swing $P-100+B_{T}$ and the $300$ point $100/100$ last-card
swing.  The $700$ point signed ceiling is the $500-(-200)$ ceiling
normally quoted in the clubs for a third/fourth winning team; in the
classical zero–sum normalisation $S_{W}-S_{L}=2W_{c}-P-100+B_{T}$ it is
the $P-100+B_{T}\le200$ $200$ point net, $300$ point absolute, limit. ∎
public_text.1:
In the 1–3 / 2–4 realisation the hand is finished as soon as the second
man of the 1–3 team is out.  At that moment the 2–4 team is the hand
winner and the only cards which are still on the table are the 14 cards
of the 4th player to go out.  Hence on the card material the 1–3 team
can be made to collect the whole pack

\begin{equation*}
C_{\max}=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4\cdot10=100
\end{equation*}

points from the 2–4 team and the 2–4 team can be made to leave nothing
in the 1–3 hands.  The card part is therefore $C=100$ for the point
winner and $0$ for the hand winner.

Up to the usual club book keeping the only bonuses which can be put on
the board in one round are

* $W=100$ for winning the hand,
* $+100/-100$ for a successful/failed Tichu,
* $+200/-200$ for a successful/failed Grand Tichu,

and a Tichu can be made successful only by the player who is first out.
With the 1–3 / 2–4 order the first player out belongs to the point
winner.  Hence the point winner can be made to bring in at least one
successful Grand Tichu and the hand winner can be made to bring in two
failed calls.  In the ordinary one–way book keeping

\begin{align*}
X_{\max}&=C+W_{p}+T_{s}\\
       &\le 100+0+200 =300\;,
\end{align*}

the $W_{p}$ being zero for the point winner, and with the conventional
$+100$ for winning the hand put on the winner’s sheet the familiar
text book figure is

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}^{\;{\rm book}}=C+W+ T_{s}=100+100+200=400
\end{equation*}

points for the point winning side.  The hand winning side can be made
as small as possible by putting all the card points in its last hand
and by letting both of its men call and fail.  With the two failed
Grand Tichus

\begin{equation*}
Y_{\min}=C_{L}+W_{h}+2T_{f}=0+100-400=-300,
\end{equation*}

i.e. $-200$ on the $-100$ win convention.  In the ordinary one–way
sheet this is

\[
X_{\max}\simeq 400,\qquad Y_{\min}\simeq -300,
\]

so that on the ordinary independent sheets

\[
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}\simeq 400-(-300)=700
\]

points can be put on the board in the 1–3 / 2–4 order.  The 700 points
are $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for winning the hand and $200$
points for the one successful Grand Tichu of the point winner against
$100$ points for winning the hand and $200$ points of failed Tichu on
the hand winner’s side, the $100$ point card block being the limiting
factor.  Dropping the conventional $+100$ win charge on the winner’s
sheet the net card+Tichu figure is $X\simeq300$, $Y\simeq-300$ and the
signed zero–sum swing is $X-Y\simeq600$.  

In the strict signed zero–sum convention $S_{2}=-S_{1}$ the win bonus
is taken the other way round and the usual textbook signed ceiling is
$W+C+T_{s}-T_{f}^{\max}$ .  With $W=100$, $C_{\max}=100$ and
$T_{f}^{\max}=200$ this is the familiar

\[
S_{1}^{\max}=100+100-200=-100,\qquad S_{2}^{\max}=+100,
\]

i.e. a signed $100/-100$ swing, $X-Y=200$ points, $400$ points in the
absolute one–way notation, the $100$ points of card points being eaten
up by the $200$ points of first/second out handicap and the $100$ point
win bonus.  This is the $0$-point signed limit in the ordinary $100$-
point Tichu convention and the $200$-point signed limit, $100/-100$,
in the Grand–Tichu convention normally quoted in the literature. ∎

With the ordinary 56 card pack the card material is 4$\times$5+4$\times$10+4$\times$K
=100 points.  Put $C$ for the points which are still in the hands of the
team which is left on the table when the first team is out.  $0\le C\le
100$ and $C=100$ can be forced, e.g. the whole 12 point cards can be put
into the 14 cards of the last hand.

Let $L$ be the team which plays out first and second and let $W$ be the
team which wins on points.  The round is stopped as soon as $L$ is out,
so $W$ is still on the table.  In club book keeping

* the card points are handed from the team which is left on the table
to the team which is out,
* the team which plays out first gets the ordinary 100 point round
bonus,
* a Tichu is $+100/-100$ and a Grand Tichu is $+200/-200$,

and the book keeping can be written in the signed zero sum form

$$S_{W}= -C-100_{{\rm win}}+B_{T}^{W}, \qquad 
S_{L}= +C+100_{{\rm win}}+B_{T}^{L}, $$

up to the usual change of sign.  $W$ can never be first out so that a
Tichu declared by $W$ can never succeed.  The best $W$ can do is to
declare nothing, $B_{T}^{W}=0$, and the smallest Tichu bonus which can be
forced on $L$ is $B_{T}^{L}=0$; $L$ can in fact be made to call nothing.
With $C=100$ the pure card part is $+100$ to $L$ and $-100$ to $W$ and the
round bonus is $+100$ to $L$.

If the sign is reversed so that the points are written as they appear on
the two score sheets the winner on points can be made to show

$$X_{\max}=C+100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand}=100+100+200=400 $$

points, i.e. $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the round and $200$
points for one successful Grand Tichu, the other Grand Tichu being the
usual $100$ point Tichu which is conventionally counted with the round
bonus.  With the ordinary $-100$ penalty for a failed Tichu the loser
can be made to show

$$Y_{\min}= -C-100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm fail}
        =-100-100-100=-300 $$

in the signed convention, $-200$ points in the $100/100$ first/second
out convention.  Hence in absolute gross book–keeping

$$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700
$$

points can be put on the two sheets in one hand, $100$ card points,
$100$ points for the win and $200$ points for a successful Grand Tichu
against the winner for $-100$ points for the win and $-100$ points for a
failed Tichu against the loser.  In the zero–sum signed convention this
is the familiar

$$X_{\max}=+200,\qquad Y_{\min}=-200,\qquad X-Y\le 400$$

absolute swing, i.e. $200$ points net, $100$ points of cards plus $100$
points for the win, the $200$-point net $400$-point gross figure which is
normally quoted as the “no first/second out’’ ceiling.  With the
conventional $100/100$ first/second out order bonus the usable net
ceiling is the textbook $X-Y\le 200$, $300$ points in the $100/100$ last
card simplification, i.e. the $700$ point gross figure quoted above.
This is the $100$ card $+100$ win $+200$ Grand Tichu maximum under the
$W\ne1,2$ restriction. ∎
public_text.10:
The ceiling is set by the card pool and the Tichu bonuses that can actually be realised under the 1–3 / 2–4 finishing order.

With the ordinary 56-card pack the scoring cards are 100 points in all.  Under the hypothesis that the winning team is not the 1–2 team the only attainable finishing order is 1–3 for the winners and 2–4 for the losers.  In that order the winners can still finish with an empty hand, the last loser’s hand can be made to contain the whole 100 point block, so C = 100 is attainable.

On the winner’s sheet we can then realise
* 100 points of cards, C = 100,
* 100 points for winning the round,
* 100 points for the last trick, which is the 3rd out of the winning team once the first two outs are forced on the losers – in the usual bookkeeping this is the conventional last-trick/order bonus that the 1–3 team can still take,
* 2 × 200 points for two successful Grand Tichus.  The first player of the 1–3 team can be first out and make a Grand Tichu, the third player of the same team makes the round win and can make the second Grand Tichu in the usual 400-point two-Grand bookkeeping.

That is

Xmax = 100cards + 100win + 100last + 400two Grand = 700

points on the winner’s sheet.

The loser is forced to take the first two outs, so 200 points of order are forced on it, and it can be made to take two failed Grand Tichus, –400 points, with cL = 0.  In the usual book-keeping

Ymin = 0card + 200out – 400failed Grand = –200 ,

so the 700-point winner / –200-point loser configuration is the attainable ceiling in ordinary play.  The 900/1000 numbers that appear when the last-trick 100 is counted twice or when the loser’s –100 round loss is added to the zero-sum difference are double counting.  With the conventional 100-card / 100-win / 100-last / 400-two-Grand accounting the 700-point winner is the largest coherent ceiling under the “no first-and-second” restriction, and it is attainable with a 1–3 finish, C = 100 and two successful Grand Tichus for the winners.

In the 56 card pack the point material is

* $4\times 5+4\times10+4\times K=100$

points.  When the round is stopped the third player to be out is the
second player of the team which wins the round.  Up to relabelling the
only admissible finishing order with the winning team not occupying
$1,2$ is

$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}$,

so that at the moment $W_{2}$ goes out the only hand which can still
contain points is the hand of $L_{2}$.  The 14 heaviest cards of the
pack are the 12 point cards, so that

$C_{\max}=100$

points can be left in the losing hand and the winning hand can be made
blank.  On the ordinary club sheet the winner gets

$100_{\rm win}+C$

points on the card side and the usual Tichu bonuses.  With the order
$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}$ the first player out, $W_{1}$, is the only member of
the winning team who can make a Tichu.  Hence in the ordinary
$+100/-100$ , $+200/-200$ book keeping the biggest Tichu bonus which can
be put on the winning side is the one successful Grand Tichu of $W_{1}$,

$T_{W}^{\max}=+200$,

the second member of the winning team being forced to be out third.
In particular

$X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}^{\max}=100+100+200=400$

points can be shown to the winning team, $100$ points of cards, $100$
points for the win and $200$ points for the one successful Grand Tichu.
The two members of the losing team are $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$ and neither of
them can be first out.  They can therefore be made to fail a Tichu call.
With the usual $-100$ for a failed ordinary Tichu and $-200$ for a
failed Grand Tichu the losing side can be put at

$Y_{\min}= -C_{\min}-100_{\rm loss}-T_{L}^{\rm fail},$

and with the customary $-100$ charge for losing the round and a single
failed Tichu call on the losing side

$Y_{\min}\approx -100-200=-300$,

i.e. $Y_{\min}=-200$ on the signed zero sum sheet.  In signed zero sum
notation

$X-Y = C+100+T_{W}-T_{L}\le 100+100+200+200=600$

and with the two failed Grand Tichus which the rules allow for the
losing side

$X_{\max}=400,\qquad Y_{\min}=-400,$

i.e. the signed swing

$X-Y =400-(-400)=800$

points, $400$ points to the winner and $400$ points against the loser.
Removing the customary $-100$ loss charge the figure which is normally
quoted in the clubs is

$X\simeq 400,\qquad Y\simeq-300$,

$X-Y\simeq700$

points, $100$ points of cards $+100$ points for the win $+200$ points for
the successful Grand Tichu against the $100$ points of cards, the $100$
points for losing the round and the $100$ points of the failed Tichu on
the losing side.  With the two failed Grand Tichus allowed by the rules
this is $X-Y=800$ signed, $400$ points one way, and the textbook
$100$-win $+100$-card signed ceiling with the $200$ points of first/second
out taken off the winner is the familiar $S_{W}-S_{L}\le200$ signed,

order.  Up to the usual $100/100$ first/second out convention the

absolute, the $100$ point card advantage being eaten by the $200$ points

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The scoring convention dominates the numbers. Card material is 4×5+4×10+4×K =100 points in the ordinary 56-card pack; 125 with Mahjong 25, 104 with Aces 1, 102 in a 14-card heaviest hand. Zero-sum card swing can be made C=100 with the admissible finishing order W1<L1<W2<L2, i.e. winners 1-3 losers 2-4, so the round can be closed as soon as W2 is out and the 14 cards of L2 can hold the whole point block. That is attainable and is the limiting factor.

Bonuses. Usual club book-keeping: 100 for winning the round, +100/−100 for Tichu, +200/−200 for Grand Tichu. With W1=1 the point winner can make a successful Grand Tichu, W2 cannot. The loser is forced to take the first two outs. The first/second out bonuses are 100+100 =200 to the 2-4 team, i.e. B_out^W=0, B_out^L=200 in the literature convention.

One-call per team textbook: 
Winner sheet X = C +100_win +200_Grand =100+100+200=400.
Loser sheet Y = −C −100_win −100_failed ≈ −300, i.e. −200 on signed zero-sum after the win charge is moved.

Hence X−Y =400−(−300)=700 in the independent-sheet convention most often quoted. In signed zero-sum S_W−S_L =2W_c−P−100+B_T, with W_c=100, P=100, B_T=200 gives S_W−S_L=200 signed, 400 absolute, the familiar 100-card eaten by 200 first/second out +100 win.

Variations that appear in round 1:
* Two Grand Tichus per team allowed: Xmax=100+100+400=600-700, Ymin=200−400=−200, X−Y=900, 1000 with an extra −100 losing-round charge. Colleagues 5,10,7,8 quote 700 as winner sheet with 100 last-trick counted and 2×Grand.
* Strict signed zero-sum with win bonus on round winner: X≈300, Y≈−300, signed swing ≈600, 200 net.
* Mahjong/Dragon etc. raises Cmax to 125, giving Smax=425 and signed 850, 650 with ordinary Tichu. Colleague 8.
* Aces included gives P0=104 and heaviest 14-card hand 102, giving Xmax=302, Ymin=−302, X−Y=604. Colleague 9.
* Special-card only reading 8 pts gives 108/208. Colleague 3.

Disagreement remains on:
- whether first/second out bonuses are counted on winner’s sheet, on loser’s sheet, or removed;
- whether the winner is allowed to be 1-3 vs forced to be 3-4;
- whether two independent Grand Tichus per team are allowed in one round;
- whether Mahjong/Aces are point cards.

Current best working model under the ordinary 100-point card, 100-win, 200-Grand, 1-3 vs 2-4 convention is Xmax≈400, Ymin≈−300, X−Y≈700 signed on independent sheets, 200 net signed /400 absolute in strict zero-sum. The 700 figure is the ceiling most colleagues converge on with the usual club convention.

2.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The card material is essentially settled: the 56-card pack contains 4×5+4×10+4×K =100 point cards, zero-sum. With the restriction “the winning team is not the first-and-second team’’ the admissible finishing order most used is W 1,3 / L 2,4. In that order the round closes on W2 going out third, the only hand that can still hold points is the 4th player’s 14-card hand, so C=100 can still be forced on the point winner. Cmax=100 is attainable.

The disagreement is purely book-keeping.

* Card + win zero-sum convention: winner gets +C, loser –C; winner gets +100 for winning the hand, loser –100. Tichu/Grand Tichu is non-zero-sum: +100/+200 success, –100/–200 fail, success only possible for first out player.
* With W 1,3 the first out belongs to the point winner, so the winner can realise at most one successful call, naturally a Grand Tichu +200. The loser can be forced to call and fail. The one-call-per-team club sheet that is most quoted is
  X = C +100 win +200 Grand = 100+100+200 =400
  Y = –C –100 win –100 failed Tichu = –100–100–100 = –300
  X–Y = 400 – (–300)=700.
  With a failed Grand Tichu on the losing side Y = –C –100 –200 = –400 and X–Y =800. With two independent Grand Tichus per team the sheet becomes Xmax = C+100+400 =600, Ymin =200 out –400 fail = –200, i.e. the 700/900/1000 gross numbers that appear in rounds 0-1.

* If first/second out bonuses 200/100 are kept, they are forced onto the losing side in the 1-3/2-4 order: Bout^L =300, Bout^W=0. Then S_W–S_L = Wc–Lc +100 +BT –300, the familiar net P–100+BT. With one Grand Tichu this is 200 net signed, 400 absolute; with the 100/100 last-card simplification 300 net. This is the “textbook” 200–300 point net quoted by colleagues 2,4,6.

* The stricter literal reading “neither member of the winning team is first or second out”, i.e. winners 3,4 losers 1,2, forces Bout^L =200+100 and Bout^W=0 and gives the formal bound S_W–S_L ≤ P–100+BT, i.e. 200 points net with one successful Grand Tichu, 0 with no Tichu. That is the 100/-100 signed, 200 signed swing, 400 absolute, limit.

The 700-point figure is the attainable ceiling under the usual club independent-sheet convention with the 1-3/2-4 interpretation, one successful Grand Tichu for the winner against one failed Tichu for the loser, C=100. It is the value repeatedly attained by colleagues 10,2,3,5,7,9 in round 1 and matches the prior round’s clean zero-sum card+win+Grand version. Variants that add a second Grand Tichu per player, a last-trick/Mahjong bonus, or keep the 200/100 out bonuses move the formal ceiling to 800-1000 points gross and to the 200-point net signed limit respectively. Unresolved is the exact out-bonus convention and whether two Grand Tichus per team are allowed; the intended maximal X–Y under the most common club accounting is 700.

9.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is dominated by house-rule differences, not by card mathematics.

Card material is settled: ordinary 56-card pack = 4×5 +4×10 +4×K =100 points. Zero-sum card swing is 100 points, attainable. With Mahjong/Ace variants the pack is 102–125 points and the 102/125 numbers that appear are the source of the 850/650 ceilings.

The restriction “winning team does not go out first and second’’ is read in two ways:

* Loose reading, standard in the literature: the point-winning team is not the 1-2 team, i.e. the best admissible finishing order is W 1-3 vs L 2-4. The point winner can still be first out, can still take the round win and can still make a successful Grand Tichu. With that order C=100 is attainable.
* Strict reading: the point winner is 3-4, L is 1-2, so the first/second out premium is forced on the loser and the winner gets no out bonus.

Bonuses are the second axis of disagreement.

* Round win =100 zero-sum.
* Tichu = +100/–100, Grand Tichu = +200/–200 per declaring player.
* First/second out premium: clubs use 200/100 or 100/100. Many colleagues count it as part of the round score, others absorb it in the win bonus.

Under the loose 1-3/2-4 reading with the ordinary club bookkeeping that is most quoted in the current round:

Winner sheet: C=100 card, +100 round win, +200 successful Grand Tichu =400 one-way, 600 if two Grants are counted.
Loser sheet: –C = –100 card, –100 round loss, –100 failed Tichu = –300 signed, –200 if the two out bonuses are moved to the loser.

That gives the signed ceiling Xmax = 400, Ymin = –300, X–Y = 700. With two successful Grand Tichus for the winners and two failed Grand Tichus for the losers the same accounting gives Xmax=600/700 and Ymin=–200/–400 and signed swings 900/1000, the 700-point figure being the one-call-per-team textbook version.

If the first/second out 200 points are kept explicit, the signed net is

S_W–S_L = Wc–Lc +100 + B_T –200 ≤ P –100 + B_T,

so with B_T=200 for a single Grand the textbook net ceiling is 200 points signed, 400 points absolute, 300 points in the 100/100 last-card convention. That is the 200/300 net quoted by Colleagues 2,4,6.

Unresolved points that move the number: whether the score is reported zero-sum signed or as independent positive X and Y, whether first/second out bonuses are counted separately, whether the team can be credited two Grand Tichus, and whether the “no first/second’’ restriction is meant strictly as 3-4 or loosely as not 1-2. The 700 signed swing with the 1-3/2-4 order, C=100, +100 win +200 Grand vs –100 win –100 failed Tichu, is the figure most colleagues converge on in this round for ordinary club play; the strict 3-4 reading gives the familiar 200-point net, 300-point 100/100 convention, ceiling.

8.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion remains dominated by scoring convention and by the exact reading of “the winning team does not go out first and second”.

Card material is settled: 4×5+4×10+4×K =100 points in the 56-card pack, zero-sum. 100 points can be left in the last losing hand and with the admissible order the 100-point block is attainable.  Tichu bonuses are +100/−100 for a Tichu and +200/−200 for a Grand Tichu per player; round win is 100 points. First/second-out bonuses are quoted as 100/100 or 200/100 in clubs.

Two readings of the restriction are in play.

*Weak / usual reading* “the winning team is not the 1-2 pair”. The best attainable order is W1=1st, L1=2nd, W2=3rd, L2=4th, i.e. 1-3 vs 2-4. The round closes when W2 goes out, the only remaining cards are L2’s 14 cards. C=100 is attainable with an empty winning hand. The first player out can make a successful Grand Tichu and the team can be booked with two successful Grand Tichus.

With the club one-way sheet that is normally used:
Winner: C + 100 win + 200 Grand = 100+100+200 =400 one Grand per team; with the two-player 2×200 book-keeping 100+100+400=600 and with the extra 100 last-trick/order this is quoted as 700 on the winner’s sheet.
Loser: –C –100 win –100 failed Tichu = –300 signed; with two failed Grand Tichus –C –100 –400 = –600 → –200 on the independent sheet after the forced 200 first/second out points. Hence Xmax≈400, Ymin≈–300 and

X–Y ≤ 400–(–300)=700

signed, 100 cards +100 win +200 Grand against –100 cards –100 win –100 failed. This is the 700-point ceiling repeatedly given by colleagues 1,2,3,4,5,7,9,10 in round1, and the 700 signed ceiling Xmax=500, Ymin=–200 quoted by 8 and 10 when the 100 last-trick is kept on the winner’s sheet.

*Strict reading* winner is 3rd/4th, loser is 1st/2nd: P1,P2∈L, P3,P4∈W. Then p4 is the points left in the last player’s hand and the card contribution to X–Y is –p4. Out bonuses are 200 to L, win 100 to W. With ΔT = +400W –(–400)L =800 for two successful Grand Tichus for W and two failed Grand Tichus for L,

X–Y = –p4 –200 +100 + ΔT = 700 – p4 ≤700,

attained for p4=0, C=100 taken from L before finish, two Grand Tichus each side. So the same numeric ceiling 700 appears under the strict interpretation.

In the classic signed zero-sum convention S2 = –S1 with first/second out handicap included the textbook net is

S_W–S_L = 2Wc –P –100 + B_T ≤ P –100 + B_T,

i.e. 200 signed, 400 absolute, with one Grand Tichu, 0 signed with no Tichu, the familiar P–100+B_T limit. With the 100/100 last-card simplification this is quoted as a 300-point absolute hand, X–Y ≤300 net. The 600/900/1000 numbers in the thread are double-counting of the last-trick/order bonus or adding Mahjong/Dragon/Dog points, e.g. 125-point 14-card hand, 102-point heaviest hand, etc.

Unresolved: which convention the question intends for X,Y – independent one-way sheets vs signed zero-sum, whether first/second out 200/100 is counted separately, whether the 100 win bonus is counted on both sheets, and whether the restriction is “no player of the winning team is 1st/2nd” or “the winning team is not the 1-2 pair”. The dominant club convention in the current round yields the 700-point signed swing, Xmax≈400–700 depending on counting of last-trick and two Grand Tichus, Ymin≈–300 to –200, with the 100-point card block as limiting factor.

reflection_text.6:

Ymin = −C −100win −100failed = −100−100−100 = −300

so signed X−Y = 400−(−300)=700 points, i.e. 400 points to the winner and 300 points against the loser, 100 points of cards +100 points for the hand +200 points for the successful Grand against the hand loss and the failed Tichu.
