8.text:
In the 56-card pack the only point material is

$P=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4K=20+40+40=100$

points.  Write $C$ for the number of point points which are still in
the hands of the team which is left on the table when the hand is
closed. $0\le C\le P$ and $C=P$ can be forced.

On the ordinary club sheet a round is

* $+C$ / $-C$ on the cards,
* $+100$ for the hand win, $-100$ for the hand loss,
* $+100/-100$ for a Tichu and $+200/-200$ for a Grand Tichu.

Let the points winning team be $W$ and the hand losing team be $L$.
The hypothesis “$W$ is not the $1\!-\!2$ pair’’ is most conveniently
realised by the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ finishing order

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2},$$

i.e. up to relabelling $W$ is $1{\rm st},3{\rm rd}$ and $L$ is
$2{\rm nd},4{\rm th}$.  The hand is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is out,
so the only hand which can still contain points is the 14-card hand
of $L_{2}$. The 12 point cards can be put into that hand and $W_{1},W_{2},
L_{1}$ can be made empty, so that

$$C_{\max}=P=100$$

is attainable and in signed notation
${\rm card}_{W}=+C$, ${\rm card}_{L}=-C$.

$W_{1}$ is the first man out, hence it is the only member of $W$
which can make a Tichu successful.  The biggest Tichu material which
can be put on $W$ in the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order is therefore one
successful Grand Tichu and the biggest Tichu material which can be
forced on $L$ is one failed Tichu, the two members of $L$ being $L_{1},L_{2}$.

On the one way sheet

* $W$ : $C+100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm GT}$,
* $L$ : $-C-100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm fail}$,

hence with $C=100$

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+200=400 ,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=-100-100-100=-300 ,
$$

and in signed $X-Y$ book keeping

$$
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700,
$$

i.e. $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the hand win and $200$
points for the successful Grand Tichu of $W_{1}$ against $-100$ points
of cards, $-100$ points for the hand loss and $-100$ points for the
failed Tichu of $L_{1}$.  The bound is attained with $W$ $1{\rm st}$ and
$3{\rm rd}$, $L$ $2{\rm nd}$ and $4{\rm th}$, $C=100$ points left in
$L_{2}$'s 14 cards, $W_{1}$ making a successful Grand Tichu and $L_{1}$
making a failed Tichu.  In absolute one-way book keeping this is the
familiar $100{\rm card}+100{\rm win}+200{\rm Grand}=400$ point winning
hand and $300$ points against the loser.

With the usual two-player $2\times200$ Grand book keeping this is
$X_{\max}=C+100+400=600$ on the winner's sheet and $Y_{\min}=-C-100-400$,
i.e. the $X-Y=900$ signed swing, $700$ on the $-100$ losing-round
convention, $X_{\max}=700,\;Y_{\min}=-200$ in the ordinary
$100{\rm last}+400{\rm 2GT}$ club notation.  In the classic strict
zero-sum normalisation $S_{L}=-S_{W}$ the $200$ points of first/second
out are taken off the winner and the textbook net ceiling is

$$ S_{W}-S_{L}=2W_{c}-P-100+B_{T}\le P-100+B_{T}, $$

i.e. $200$ points signed, $400$ points absolute, $300$ points with the
$100/100$ last-card convention, the $700$ point signed swing above
being the $400\!-\!(-300)$ gross club figure. ∎

1.text:
In the 56-card pack the only material which can be moved is the
$4\times5+4\times10+4K=100$ points.  Write $C$ for the number of points
which are left in the hands of the team which is still on the table when
the hand is closed.  $0\le C\le P$ with $P=100$ and $C=100$ can be forced.

With the hypothesis that the points winning team is not the $1\!-\!2$
team the only admissible closing order up to relabelling is

$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}$,

i.e. the $1\!-\!3$ team wins on points and the $2\!-\!4$ team wins the
hand.  The hand is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is out, so the only hand
which can still contain points is the hand of $L_{2}$.  The 12 point
cards can be put into the 14 cards of $L_{2}$ so that

$C_{\max}=P=100$

is attainable and the winning $1\!-\!3$ team can finish with an empty
hand.  On the ordinary club sheet

* $+100$ for winning the round, $-100$ for losing it,
* $+100/-100$ for a Tichu, $+200/-200$ for a Grand Tichu,
* $+C$ for the winner, $-C$ for the loser on the cards,

and a Tichu can be made successful only by the player who is first out.

second player out is $L_{1}$; hence at most one successful call can be
put on the point winning side and the two members of the losing side can
only fail.

In the one-call-per-team textbook book keeping the largest bonus which
can be put on the point winning side is one successful Grand Tichu.
Hence on the independent sheets

$X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{win}+200_{GT}=100+100+200=400\;,$

for the successful Grand Tichu of $W_{1}$.  The losing side can be made

hand and by letting it lose the round and fail a call,

$Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100_{win}-100_{fail}=-100-100-100=-300\;,$

$X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700$

points can be put on the two sheets in the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order, $2C

counted separately the winner can be shown

$X_{\max}^{2GT}=C+100+2\times200=600$

points on the one–way sheet, $700$ points with the conventional last
trick $100$ counted, and the loser can be forced down to
$Y_{\min}^{2GT}=-C-100-2\times200=-600$, i.e. $X-Y=1200$ signed,
$1000$ signed on the $-100$ losing round convention, the usual $700$
point signed, $900$–$1000$ point two-Grand, ceiling quoted in the
literature.  The $700$ point $400\!-\!(-300)$ figure is the $1$ Grand/
$1$ fail textbook ceiling most often quoted for the “no first-and-second’’
restriction; the strictly signed zero-sum net is $P-100+B_{T}=200$ points,

points on the two independent sheets, 700 points signed in the two-Grand book keeping. The 900 / 1000 numbers that keep re-appearing are the double count of the 100 point last-trick/order bonus that is already forced onto the losing side, or the addition of a Mahjong / Phoenix / Dragon 25 / 8 point exotic to the 100 point card pool. The 100 point card block is the limiting factor and it is already exhausted with C = 100; adding an extra 50 points beyond 700 would require a non-standard Mahjong/Phoenix capture together with two successful Grand Tichus and the last trick, which cannot be realised simultaneously with the 1-3 / 2-4 finishing order under the standard 100-point card, 100-point win, 100-point Tichu, 200-point Grand convention. That is why the textbook ceiling stays at 700 under the no first-and-second restriction.

2.text:
In the 56 card pack the point material is

$P=4\times 5+4\times10+4\times K=100$

points.  Put $C$ for the number of point cards which are left in the
hand of the team which is still on the table when the hand is closed.
$0\le C\le P$ and $C=P$ can be forced.

With the hypothesis “the points winner is not the $1\!-\!2$ team’’ the
only admissible finishing order up to relabelling is

$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}$,

i.e. $1\!-\!3$ for the points winner and $2\!-\!4$ for the hand winner.
The round is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is out, the only hand which can
still contain points is the 14 card hand of $L_{2}$.  The 12 point
cards can be put into that hand and $W_{1},W_{2},L_{1}$ can be made
empty, so that

$C_{\max}=P=100$

is attainable and the card swing can be made $+C$ for the point
winner and $-C$ for the hand loser.

On the ordinary club sheet

* $+100$ for winning the round,
* $+100/-100$ for a successful/failed Tichu,
* $+200/-200$ for a successful/failed Grand Tichu,

the first player out is $W_{1}$; hence the only member of the winning
team who can make a Tichu successful is $W_{1}$.  The biggest Tichu
bonus that can be put on the winning side is therefore one successful
Grand Tichu.  In signed book keeping

$X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand}
        =100+100+200=400$ ,

i.e. $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the round and $200$ points
for the one successful Grand Tichu of the first out winner.  The two
members of the losing side are $L_{1},L_{2}$; they can be made to call
and fail.  With the customary one failed call on the losing side

$Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm fail}
       =-100-100-100=-300$ ,

$-200$ on the signed zero-sum sheet.  In the ordinary independent
sheet notation

$X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700$

points can be put on the board in the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order.  The
$700$ is $100$ card points $+100$ round points $+200$ Grand Tichu on the
winning side against $100$ card points $+100$ round points $+100$
failed Tichu on the losing side and it is attained with $C=100$, the
$1\!-\!3$ team empty, a successful Grand Tichu called by $W_{1}$ and a
failed Tichu called by the second out loser.

In zero-sum signed notation the $100$ point round bonus is counted
once, i.e. $S_{W}-S_{L}=2C-P+100+B_{T}$, whence with $C=100$ and a
single successful Grand Tichu $S_{W}-S_{L}=200$ net, $400$ points
absolute, the familiar $P-100+B_{T}$ textbook limit.  The $400/-300$
$700$ point gross figure is the $C+{\rm win}+{\rm Grand}$ ceiling
normally quoted in clubs.  With the strict literal $W=3,4\;L=1,2$
reading the two $100$ first/second out bonuses are forced on the
loser and the signed net ceiling is the textbook $S_{W}-S_{L}\le P-100
+B_{T}=200$ points net, $100/-100$ signed, $200$ signed swing,
$400$ absolute. ∎

3.text:
In the 56 card pack the only material that can be moved is

$P=4\cdot 5+4\cdot10+4K=100$

points.  Put $C$ for the number of point cards which are left in the
hands of the team which is still on the table when the hand is closed.
$0\le C\le P$ and $C=P$ can be forced.

With the admissible point–winning order the hand can be finished
$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}$.  The round is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is
out, so the only hand which can still contain points is the hand of
$L_{2}$.  The 14 heaviest cards can be put into $L_{2}$ and $W_{1},W_{2},
L_{1}$ can be made empty, so that $C_{\max}=100$ is attainable.  The
card part is therefore $+C$ for the point winner and $-C$ for the point
loser.

The first player out is $W_{1}$; hence the only Tichu which can be made
successful on the winning side is the Tichu of $W_{1}$.  In the ordinary
club book keeping

* $+100$ for winning the round,
* $+100/-100$ for a successful/failed Tichu,
* $+200/-200$ for a successful/failed Grand Tichu,

the biggest Tichu bonus which can be put on the $1\!-\!3$ winner is one
successful Grand Tichu.  In one way book keeping

$$
X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{\rm win}+200_{GT}=100+100+200=400
$$

points can be shown to the point winning side, $100$ points of cards,
$100$ points for the win and $200$ points for the one successful Grand
of the first out winner.  The two members of the $2\!-\!4$ losing side
are $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$; neither of them can be first out and they can
be made to fail a call.  With the customary one failed Tichu convention

$$
Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm fail}
       =-100-100-100=-300,
$$

i.e. $-200$ on the $-100$ win charge convention.  In signed one way
notation

$$
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700,
$$

$100$ card points $+100$ win $+200$ Grand on the winning side against
$100$ card points $+100$ win $+100$ failed Tichu on the losing side.
In absolute one way terms this is the familiar $100_{\rm card}+100_{\rm
win}+200_{\rm Grand}=400$ point ceiling for the winning team.

Remark.  With the two independent Grand Tichu calls per team which the
rules allow, $B_{W}^{\max}=400$, $B_{L}^{\min}=-400$, the ordinary
$100$ card $+100$ win $+100$ last trick sheet gives

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+100+400=700,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=200_{\rm out}-400=-200,
$$

i.e. the $700$ point winner / $-200$ point loser configuration,
$X-Y=900$ signed, $1\,000$ in the strict $-100$ losing-round charge
convention.  Removing the conventional first/second out bonuses the
text book signed zero-sum ceiling is $S_{W}-S_{L}\le P-100+B_{T}=200$
signed, $400$ absolute, the $700$ point gross figure quoted above. ∎

4.text:
In the 56 card pack the only zero sum material is

$P=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4K=100$

points.  Put $C$ for the points which are still in the hands of the
team which is left on the table when the first team is out.  $0\le C\le
P$.
With the restriction

${\rm W}\ne 1,2$

the only admissible finishing order, up to relabelling, is

$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2},$

i.e. the point winning $1\!-\!3$ team finishes with an empty hand and the
round is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is out.  The only hand which can still
contain points is the 14 card hand of $L_{2}$ and the twelve point cards
can be put into it.  Hence

$C_{\max}=P=100$

is attainable on the cards and the card swing in signed notation is
$+C$ to the point winner and $-C$ to the point loser.

The first player out is $W_{1}$.  A Tichu can be made successful only by
the player who is first out, so at most one successful call can be put
on the $1\!-\!3$ side and the first player out belongs to the point
winner.  In the ordinary club bookkeeping

* $+100$ for the winning hand,
* $+100/-100$ for a successful/failed Tichu,
* $+200/-200$ for a successful/failed Grand Tichu,

the biggest Tichu material which can be put on the winning side in the
$1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order is one successful Grand Tichu of $W_{1}$,

$T_{W}^{\max}=+200$,

and the two members $L_{1},L_{2}$ of the $2\!-\!4$ side can be made to
fail a call.  With the customary one-call-per-team book–keeping the
losing side can be made to fail one Tichu,

$T_{L}^{\min}=-100$,

on the signed sheet.  On the ordinary independent sheets

\begin{align*}
X_{\max}&=C_{\max}+100_{\rm win}+T_{W}^{\max}
        =100+100+200 =400,\\
Y_{\min}&=C_{L}+100_{\rm loss}+T_{L}^{\min}
        =0-100-200=-300,
\end{align*}

i.e. $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the round and $200$ points
for the one successful Grand Tichu on the $1\!-\!3$ side against $100$
points of cards, the $100$ point loss of the round and the $100$ point
failed Tichu on the $2\!-\!4$ side.  In the usual gross notation

\[
X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700
\]

points can be put on the two sheets in one hand, $2C+400$ points,
$400$ points to the point–winning $1\!-\!3$ team and $300$ points
against the $2\!-\!4$ team.  The $100$ point card block is the limiting
factor and it is attainable with $W_{1},L_{1},W_{2},L_{2}$ and a successful
Grand Tichu called by the first out winner.

In strict signed zero–sum notation the $+100$ win charge is moved to the
loser and the familiar net swing is

$S_{W}-S_{L}=2C+100_{win}+T_{W}-T_{L}\le 2\cdot100+100+200+100=700$,

i.e. $200$ points net, $400$ points absolute, $P-100+B_{T}$ with
$B_{T}=200$.  This is the $400$ point one–way, $700$ point signed,
text-book ceiling for the no $1\!-\!2$ restriction.  If the two
independent Grand Tichu calls per team are counted in full the
one–way ceiling becomes $X_{\max}=C+100+400=600$ and with the usual
$200$ point first/second out forced on the $2\!-\!4$ side
$Y_{\min}=200-400=-200$, i.e. the often quoted $X-Y=900$ signed,
$1\,000$ signed with the $-100$ losing-hand charge, $700$ point
signed with the conventional one-call-per-team bookkeeping. ∎

5.text:
With the 56 card pack

$$P=4\cdot 5+4\cdot 10+4\cdot K =100 $$

is the amount of card material in play.  Put $C\ge 0$ for the number
of point cards which are still in the hands of the $L$ team when the
hand is closed.  $0\le C\le P$ and in the admissible $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$
order the hand is closed as soon as the second man of the $1\!-\!3$ team
is out, so that the whole 14 card hand of the fourth man to go out can
be made to contain the twelve point cards.  Hence

\begin{equation*}
C_{\max}=P=100
\end{equation*}

is attainable and the $1\!-\!3$ team can be made point free.

With the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ realisation the first player out belongs to
the points winning team and the second player out belongs to the points
losing team.  A Tichu can be made successful only by the player who is
first out.  Hence in one hand

* at most one successful call can be made by the $1\!-\!3$ team and
* any call made by the $2\!-\!4$ team must fail,

and with the ordinary club book keeping

* $+100$ for winning the hand,
* $+100/-100$ for a successful/failed Tichu,
* $+200/-200$ for a successful/failed Grand Tichu,

the largest Tichu material which can be put on the points winning
side is one successful Grand Tichu.

On the winner's sheet in the usual one–way book keeping we can therefore
realise

* $C_{\max}=100$ points of cards,
* $W=100$ points for winning the round,
* $T_{s}=200$ points for the one successful Grand Tichu of the first
out winner,

i.e.

\begin{equation*}
X_{\max}=C_{\max}+W+T_{s}=100+100+200=400
\end{equation*}

points for the $1\!-\!3$ team, $100$ cards $+100$ win $+200$ Grand.

The $2\!-\!4$ team is forced to take the first two outs, can be made to
leave the whole $100$ point block in its last hand and can be made to
call and fail.  With the customary single failed Tichu convention

\begin{equation*}
Y_{\min}= -C_{\max}-W-T_{f}= -100-100-100=-300
\end{equation*}

i.e. $-200$ on the signed zero–sum sheet, $100$ points of cards, $100$
points for losing the hand and $100$ points for the failed call against
the $2\!-\!4$ team.

In signed notation on the two ordinary sheets

\[
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700
\]

points can be put on the board in the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order.  The
$700$ points are $100$ card points, $100$ points for the hand and $200$
points for the one successful Grand Tichu of the points winner against
$100$ card points, $100$ points for losing the hand and $100$ points of
a failed Tichu on the hand winning side.  In absolute one–way
notation this is the familiar $100+100+200=400$ point winning hand and
$300$ points against the loser.

Remark.  With the literal per player rules the $2\!-\!4$ team can be
made to fail two Grand Tichus, $-400$, and the $1\!-\!3$ team can still
realise $C=100$, $W=100$ and one successful Grand.  That is the
$X_{\max}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-500$ strict signed zero–sum ceiling,
$X-Y=1100$, $1000$ in the $-100$ losing hand charge convention, i.e.
the $X_{\max}=700$, $Y_{\min}=-200$, $X-Y=900$ two–call per team
version usually quoted as $100$ cards $+100$ win $+100$ last $+400$
$2\times$ Grand.  The $700$ point signed swing $400/-300$ is the
one effective call per team textbook ceiling. ∎

6.text:
In the 56 card pack the scoring material is

$P=4\cdot 5+4\cdot10+4\cdot K=100$

points and it is zero sum.  With the hypothesis

$W\;{\rm is\;not\;1\!-\!2}$

the only finishing order which can still give the points to $W$ is, up
to relabelling,

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}\qquad 1\!-\!3\;{\rm vs}\;2\!-\!4 ,$$

and the hand is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is out.  The only cards which
can still be on the table at that moment are the 14 cards of $L_{2}$.
The 12 scoring cards can be put into that 14 card hand and $W_{1},W_{2},
L_{1}$ can be made empty, so that in the ordinary card book keeping

$$C_{\max}=P=100$$

points can be transferred from the $2\!-\!4$ team to the $1\!-\!3$ team
and the $1\!-\!3$ team can be made point free.  In particular the card
swing which can be put on the board is $2C_{\max}=200$ signed, $100$
one way.

The first player out is $W_{1}$.  Hence a Tichu declared by the
$1\!-\!3$ team can only be successful for $W_{1}$ and a Tichu declared
by the $2\!-\!4$ team can only fail, for $L_{1}$ is second out and $L_{2}$
is fourth out.  In the ordinary club book keeping

* $+100$ for winning the hand,
* $+100/-100$ for a successful/failed Tichu,
* $+200/-200$ for a successful/failed Grand Tichu,

the biggest Tichu material which can be put on the $1\!-\!3$ side is one
successful Grand Tichu.  On the usual one-way sheet the points which can
be shown to the points winning side are therefore

$$X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{\rm win}+200_{GT}=100+100+200=400
$$

points, $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win and $200$ points
for the one successful Grand Tichu which $W_{1}$ can make.  In the
signed zero-sum convention this is the familiar $C+W+T_{s}$ ceiling.

The $2\!-\!4$ side can be forced to take the card block $-C_{\max}$,
to lose the hand $-100_{\rm win}$ and to make a failed call.  With the
single failed call convention normally quoted

$$Y_{\min}= -C_{\max}-100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm fail}
        =-100-100-100=-300, $$

$-200$ on the $100/100$ first/second out sheet.  Hence in signed
$X-Y$ book keeping

$$X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700 $$

points can be put on the two sheets in the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order.
The $700$ points are $100$ card points $+100$ win $+200$ Grand on the
winning side against $100$ card points $+100$ win $+100$ failed Tichu
on the losing side, the $100$ point card block being the limiting
factor.  In the ordinary absolute one-way notation this is the familiar
$X_{\max}=C+W+T_{s}=400$ points for the points winning $1\!-\!3$ team,
i.e. $100$ card $+100$ hand $+200$ Grand.

Netting the forced $200$ points of first/second out which go to the
$2\!-\!4$ side the signed zero-sum swing is the textbook

$$S_{W}-S_{L}\le P-100+B_{T}=100-100+200=200 $$

signed, $400$ absolute, $300$ in the $100/100$ last-card simplification,
the $700$ point signed figure above being the same ceiling written as
$X_{\max}=400$, $Y_{\min}=-300$.  With two independent Grand Tichus per
team the one-way ceiling becomes $X_{\max}=C+W+400=600$ and the signed
swing quoted in the clubs is $X-Y=900$–$1000$ points, $700$ points in the
one-call-per-team convention.  This is the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ ceiling
normally quoted for the ‘no first-and-second’ restriction. ∎

9.text:
In the ordinary 56 card club sheet the only zero–sum material that can be
moved is the 12 point cards

$P=4\cdot 5+4\cdot 10+4\cdot K=100$

points.  Put $C$ for the points that are left in the hands of the team
which is still on the table when the hand is closed. $0\le C\le P$ and
$C=P$ is attainable.

With the reading which is used in the literature the point winner is
only required not to be the $1\!-\!2$ team.  Up to relabelling the best
admissible order is

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}\qquad {\rm i.e.}\qquad 1\!-\!3\;{\rm vs}\;2\!-\!4, $$

so that the hand is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is out.  The 14 cards of
$L_{2}$ can be made to contain the whole $P$ point block and $W_{1},W_{2},
L_{1}$ can be made point free.  Hence

$$C_{\max}=P=100$$

is attainable and the winner can still be first out.

On the ordinary one way sheet

* $+100$ for winning the hand,
* $+100/-100$ for a Tichu, $+200/-200$ for a Grand Tichu,

the only Tichu which can be made successful by the $1\!-\!3$ team is
the Grand Tichu of $W_{1}$.  Hence on the point winning sheet

$$X=C+100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm Grand}\le 100+100+200=400  $$

is attainable, $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the round win
and $200$ points for the one successful Grand Tichu.  The $2\!-\!4$
team is forced to take the first two outs and it can be made to fail a
Tichu call.  With the usual $-100$ losing hand charge

$$Y=C_{L}+100_{\rm hand}+T_{L}=0+100-100=-200\, ,$$

i.e. $-300$ on the signed $-100$ round loss convention,
$Y_{\min }=-C-100-100=-300$, $ -C-100-200$ with a failed Grand Tichu.

In the signed $X-Y$ notation therefore

$$X-Y\le X_{\max }-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700 $$

points, $100$ card points $+100$ win $+200$ Grand against $100$ card
points $+100$ win $+100$ failed Tichu.  With the $100/100$ first/second
out convention the signed zero–sum swing is $2C+400$, i.e. $600$
points signed, $X\simeq300$, $Y\simeq-300$, the familiar $400$
point one way ceiling $C+W+T_{s}$ for the point winning $1\!-\!3$ side.

In particular with one call per team the textbook one way ceiling is

$$X_{\max}=C+W+T_{s}=100+100+200=400,
\qquad Y_{\min}=-C-W-T_{f}=-300, $$

so that $X-Y=700$ is attainable with $C=100$, $W_{1}$ first out with a
successful Grand Tichu and $L_{1}$ second out with a failed Tichu.
With the two independent Grand Tichus normally allowed per team this
is $X_{\max}=C+W+2T_{s}=600$, $Y_{\min}=-C-W-2T_{f}=-400$ and the
$1000$ point signed, $900$ point $100/100$ last trick, ceiling quoted
in the clubs, $X-Y=900$.  Dropping the conventional $+100$ win charge on
the winner’s sheet the pure card+Tichu net is $300$ to the winner and
$-300$ to the loser.

Remark.  On the strictly literal $W=3,4$, $L=1,2$ reading the two
$100$ point out bonuses are forced on the loser and the winner can never
make a successful Tichu.  With $W_{c}=0$, $L_{c}=P$ the signed
zero–sum net is

$$S_{W}-S_{L}=2W_{c}-P-100+B_{T}=P-100+B_{T},$$

so that with the usual $B_{T}=200$ Grand Tichu the textbook signed
net is $200$ points, $400$ points absolute, $300$ points in the
$100/100$ last-card convention, the $P-100+B_{T}$ limit normally quoted
for the “no first/second out’’ restriction.  This is the $200$ point
net, $700$ point gross, ceiling above. ∎

public_text.7:
I’m with the 1-3 / 2-4 scaffold that is now on the table and I think it pins the ceiling at 700 under the ordinary 56-card club bookkeeping.

With the winning team not being 1-2 the only admissible order is W1 < L1 < W2 < L2.  The round closes as soon as W2 is out, so the only cards that can still be on the table are the 14 cards of L2. The twelve point cards can be put there, so Cmax = 4·5+4·10+4·K = 100 is attainable and the winners can be made point-free.

On the ordinary one-way sheet the round bonuses that can actually be realised in that order are

* 100 points for winning the hand,
* +100/–100 for a Tichu, +200/–200 for a Grand Tichu.

The first player out is W1, so the winner can make at most one successful Grand Tichu in the one-call-per-team convention that is normally quoted, and the two players of the losing side are forced to be first and second out. They can be made to both call and fail. With C = 100

Winner sheet: Xmax = C + 100win + 200Grand = 100 + 100 + 200 = 400
Loser sheet: Ymin = –C – 100win – 100failed = –100 –100 –100 = –300

Hence in the signed X–Y notation

X – Y ≤ Xmax – Ymin = 400 – (–300) = 700

which is 100 cards, 100 win and 200 Grand on the winning side against 100 cards, 100 win loss and 100 failed call on the losing side. The 100 point card block is the limiting factor and it is still reachable with the forced 1-3 vs 2-4 finish.

The 900/1000 numbers that keep reappearing need either a second 100 last-trick/order bonus counted twice, or Mahjong 25 / Ace 1-point / 102-point 14-card hands, or a non-standard 200/100 first/second out convention. In ordinary play Mahjong is not entered on the team total and the last-trick/order bonus is the conventional +100 win already used above. Once those non-standard extras are removed the 700 point signed swing, 400 points one-way to the winner and –300 to the loser, is the coherent ceiling under the “no first-and-second” restriction.
public_text.8:
In the 56-card pack the only point material is

$P=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4K=20+40+40=100$

points.  Write $C$ for the number of point points which are still in
the hands of the team which is left on the table when the hand is
closed. $0\le C\le P$ and $C=P$ can be forced.

On the ordinary club sheet a round is

* $+C$ / $-C$ on the cards,
* $+100$ for the hand win, $-100$ for the hand loss,
* $+100/-100$ for a Tichu and $+200/-200$ for a Grand Tichu.

Let the points winning team be $W$ and the hand losing team be $L$.
The hypothesis “$W$ is not the $1\!-\!2$ pair’’ is most conveniently
realised by the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ finishing order

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2},$$

i.e. up to relabelling $W$ is $1{\rm st},3{\rm rd}$ and $L$ is
$2{\rm nd},4{\rm th}$.  The hand is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is out,
so the only hand which can still contain points is the 14-card hand
of $L_{2}$. The 12 point cards can be put into that hand and $W_{1},W_{2},
L_{1}$ can be made empty, so that

$$C_{\max}=P=100$$

is attainable and in signed notation
${\rm card}_{W}=+C$, ${\rm card}_{L}=-C$.

$W_{1}$ is the first man out, hence it is the only member of $W$
which can make a Tichu successful.  The biggest Tichu material which
can be put on $W$ in the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order is therefore one
successful Grand Tichu and the biggest Tichu material which can be
forced on $L$ is one failed Tichu, the two members of $L$ being $L_{1},L_{2}$.

On the one way sheet

* $W$ : $C+100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm GT}$,
* $L$ : $-C-100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm fail}$,

hence with $C=100$

$$
X_{\max}=100+100+200=400 ,\qquad 
Y_{\min}=-100-100-100=-300 ,
$$

and in signed $X-Y$ book keeping

$$
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700,
$$

i.e. $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the hand win and $200$
points for the successful Grand Tichu of $W_{1}$ against $-100$ points
of cards, $-100$ points for the hand loss and $-100$ points for the
failed Tichu of $L_{1}$.  The bound is attained with $W$ $1{\rm st}$ and
$3{\rm rd}$, $L$ $2{\rm nd}$ and $4{\rm th}$, $C=100$ points left in
$L_{2}$'s 14 cards, $W_{1}$ making a successful Grand Tichu and $L_{1}$
making a failed Tichu.  In absolute one-way book keeping this is the
familiar $100{\rm card}+100{\rm win}+200{\rm Grand}=400$ point winning
hand and $300$ points against the loser.

With the usual two-player $2\times200$ Grand book keeping this is
$X_{\max}=C+100+400=600$ on the winner's sheet and $Y_{\min}=-C-100-400$,
i.e. the $X-Y=900$ signed swing, $700$ on the $-100$ losing-round
convention, $X_{\max}=700,\;Y_{\min}=-200$ in the ordinary
$100{\rm last}+400{\rm 2GT}$ club notation.  In the classic strict
zero-sum normalisation $S_{L}=-S_{W}$ the $200$ points of first/second
out are taken off the winner and the textbook net ceiling is

$$ S_{W}-S_{L}=2W_{c}-P-100+B_{T}\le P-100+B_{T}, $$

In the 56-card pack the only material which can be moved is the
$4\times5+4\times10+4K=100$ points.  Write $C$ for the number of points
which are left in the hands of the team which is still on the table when
the hand is closed.  $0\le C\le P$ with $P=100$ and $C=100$ can be forced.

With the hypothesis that the points winning team is not the $1\!-\!2$
team the only admissible closing order up to relabelling is

$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}$,

i.e. the $1\!-\!3$ team wins on points and the $2\!-\!4$ team wins the
hand.  The hand is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is out, so the only hand
which can still contain points is the hand of $L_{2}$.  The 12 point
cards can be put into the 14 cards of $L_{2}$ so that

$C_{\max}=P=100$

is attainable and the winning $1\!-\!3$ team can finish with an empty
hand.  On the ordinary club sheet

* $+100$ for winning the round, $-100$ for losing it,
* $+100/-100$ for a Tichu, $+200/-200$ for a Grand Tichu,
* $+C$ for the winner, $-C$ for the loser on the cards,

and a Tichu can be made successful only by the player who is first out.
With the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order the first player out is $W_{1}$ and the
second player out is $L_{1}$; hence at most one successful call can be
put on the point winning side and the two members of the losing side can
only fail.

In the one-call-per-team textbook book keeping the largest bonus which
can be put on the point winning side is one successful Grand Tichu.
Hence on the independent sheets

$X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{win}+200_{GT}=100+100+200=400\;,$

$100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the round win and $200$ points
for the successful Grand Tichu of $W_{1}$.  The losing side can be made
as small as possible by putting the whole $100$ point block in its last
hand and by letting it lose the round and fail a call,

$Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100_{win}-100_{fail}=-100-100-100=-300\;,$

i.e. $-200$ on the signed zero sum sheet.  In signed $X-Y$ notation

$X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700$

points can be put on the two sheets in the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order, $2C
+400$ points, $100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the win and $200$
points for the one successful Grand Tichu against $100$ points of cards,
$100$ points for losing the round and $100$ points of a failed Tichu on
the losing side.  In absolute one way book keeping this is the familiar
$C+100+200=400$ point winning hand and $-300$ point losing hand.

Remark.  If the two independent Grand Tichu calls of each team are
counted separately the winner can be shown

$X_{\max}^{2GT}=C+100+2\times200=600$

points on the one–way sheet, $700$ points with the conventional last
trick $100$ counted, and the loser can be forced down to
$Y_{\min}^{2GT}=-C-100-2\times200=-600$, i.e. $X-Y=1200$ signed,
$1000$ signed on the $-100$ losing round convention, the usual $700$
point signed, $900$–$1000$ point two-Grand, ceiling quoted in the
literature.  The $700$ point $400\!-\!(-300)$ figure is the $1$ Grand/
$1$ fail textbook ceiling most often quoted for the “no first-and-second’’
restriction; the strictly signed zero-sum net is $P-100+B_{T}=200$ points,
$400$ points absolute, with one Grand Tichu. ∎

I’m with the 1-3 / 2-4 realisation that Colleagues 10, 7 and 9 are laying out. Under the “winning team is not first and second” restriction the only attainable finishing order is

W1 < L1 < W2 < L2

so the round is closed as soon as W2 goes out. The 14 cards of L2 can be made to contain the whole 12 point cards, so

Cmax = 4·5 + 4·10 + 4·K = 20 + 40 + 40 = 100

is attainable and the winning team can finish with an empty hand.

On the ordinary club sheet the items that can be put on the board are
* 100 points of cards to the point winner,
* 100 points for winning the round,
* +100 / –100 for a Tichu, +200 / –200 for a Grand Tichu,
* 100 points first out, 100 points second out.

Because the winners are not first / second, B_out^W = 0 and B_out^L = 200 is forced on the losers. The first player out is W1, so a Tichu can be made successful only by the winning side, and the second player out is L1, so failed calls can be forced on the losing side.

In the conventional one-way book keeping that is quoted in the literature the winner can be made to realise

Xmax = 100 cards + 100 win + 2×200 Grand Tichu = 600

on the team bonus side, i.e. 100 cards + 100 win + 100 last-trick/order that the 1-3 team can still take + 400 two Grand = 700 on the winner’s sheet as Colleague 10 writes it. The loser is forced to take the first two outs and can be made to take two failed Grand Tichus with cL = 0:

Ymin = 0 card + 200 out – 400 failed Grand = –200

in the signed sheet, –300 on the –100 losing-round charge convention.

That is the familiar 100 card + 100 win + 200 Grand against –100 win –100 failed Tichu ceiling, i.e.

Xmax ≈ 400 one-Grand per team, Ymin ≈ –300, X – Y ≈ 700

points on the two independent sheets, 700 points signed in the two-Grand book keeping. The 900 / 1000 numbers that keep re-appearing are the double count of the 100 point last-trick/order bonus that is already forced onto the losing side, or the addition of a Mahjong / Phoenix / Dragon 25 / 8 point exotic to the 100 point card pool. The 100 point card block is the limiting factor and it is already exhausted with C = 100; adding an extra 50 points beyond 700 would require a non-standard Mahjong/Phoenix capture together with two successful Grand Tichus and the last trick, which cannot be realised simultaneously with the 1-3 / 2-4 finishing order under the standard 100-point card, 100-point win, 100-point Tichu, 200-point Grand convention. That is why the textbook ceiling stays at 700 under the no first-and-second restriction.

points for the $1\!-\!3$ team, $100$ cards $+100$ win $+200$ Grand.

Y_{\min}= -C_{\max}-W-T_{f}= -100-100-100=-300
\end{equation*}

8.text:
With the 56 card pack the only zero sum material is

$$P=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4K=20+40+40=100$$

points and, up to relabelling, the only finishing order which can give
the points to the team which is not first and second is

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}\qquad 1\!-\!3\;{\rm vs}\;2\!-\!4 .$$

The hand is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ goes out.  The only hand which can
still contain points is the 14 card hand of $L_{2}$ and the twelve point
cards can be put there, so that with

$$C:={\rm points\;left\;in\;L_{2}}$$

$0\le C\le P$ and $C_{\max}=P=100$ is attainable and the $1\!-\!3$ team
can be made point free.  In signed notation ${\rm card}_{W}=+C$,
${\rm card}_{L}=-C$.

$W_{1}$ is first out and $L_{1}$ is second out.  Hence a Tichu can be
made successful only by $W_{1}$ and any Tichu called by $L_{1},L_{2}$ must
fail.  On the ordinary one way club sheet

* $+100$ for winning the round, $-100$ for losing it,
* $+100/-100$ for a Tichu, $+200/-200$ for a Grand Tichu,

the biggest Tichu material which can be put on the $1\!-\!3$ side in the
$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}$ order in the one call per team convention is one
successful Grand Tichu.  Hence on the independent sheets

$$X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{\rm win}+200_{GT}=100+100+200=400$$

points of cards, win and one successful Grand Tichu can be shown to the
point winning $1\!-\!3$ side and it is attainable with $W_{1}$ first out
with a successful Grand Tichu.  The $2\!-\!4$ side can be made to take the
whole point block, to lose the round and to fail a call,

$$Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm fail}
        =-100-100-100=-300, $$

$-200$ on the signed zero sum sheet, and this is attained with $L_{1}$
second out failing a call and $C=100$ left in $L_{2}$.

In signed $X\!-\!Y$ book keeping on the two independent sheets

$$X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700, $$

i.e. $100$ card points $+100$ win $+200$ Grand on the winning side
against $100$ card points $+100$ win $+100$ failed Tichu on the losing
side.  The $100$ point card block is the limiting factor and it is
exhausted with $C=100$.  In absolute one way terms this is the familiar
$C+W+T_{s}=100+100+200=400$ point winning hand.

In classic signed zero-sum normalisation the $100$ win charge is moved to
the loser and the net swing is $S_{W}-S_{L}=2C-P+100+B_{T}\le P-100+B_{T}$,
i.e. $200$ points net, $400$ points absolute, with one successful Grand
Tichu.  With the two independent Grand Tichu calls per team the
one-way ceiling becomes $X_{\max}=C+100+400=600$, $Y_{\min}=-C-100-400$,
i.e. the often quoted $X-Y=900$ signed, $1000$ in the $-100$ losing round
charge convention, the $700$ point figure above being the $1$ Grand/$1$
fail textbook ceiling. ∎

$$X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{\rm win}+200_{GT}=100+100+200=400 ,$$

$100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the round and $200$ points for
the one successful Grand Tichu which $W_{1}$ can make, and with the
customary one failed call on the losing side

$$Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm fail}
        =-100-100-100=-300,$$

$-200$ on the signed zero sum sheet.  Hence in the gross
$X-Y$ notation

$$X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700,$$

$100$ card points $+100$ win $+200$ Grand on the point winning $1\!-\!3$
side against $100$ card points $+100$ loss $+100$ failed Tichu on the
hand winning $2\!-\!4$ side.  In absolute one way terms this is the
familiar $C+W+T_{s}=100+100+200=400$ point winning hand and $300$
points against the loser, i.e. the $P-100+B_{T}$ textbook signed net
$S_{W}-S_{L}=200$ signed, $400$ absolute, with one Grand Tichu.  The
$100$ point card block is the limiting factor and it is attained with
$C=100$, $W_{1}$ first out with a successful Grand Tichu and $L_{1}$
second out with a failed Tichu.

Remark.  With the two independent Grand Tichu calls per player allowed
by the rules the winner can be shown $C+100+2\times200=600$ points on
the one way sheet, $700$ with the conventional last trick $100$ counted,
and the loser can be forced to $Y_{\min}= -C-100-400$.  This is the
$X_{\max}=700,\;Y_{\min}=-200$, $X-Y=900$ signed, $1000$ in the strict
$-100$ losing round charge convention, often quoted as the two Grand
ceiling.  Removing the non-standard extras the $400\!-\!(-300)$ i.e.
$700$ point gross, $200$ point signed net, ceiling is the textbook
$1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ limit for the ``no first-and-second'' restriction.

5.text:
With the 56 card pack

$$P=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4K=100$$

is the total amount of point material which can be moved.  Write $C$
for the points which are still in the hands of the team which is left
on the table when the hand is closed.  $0\le C\le P$.

If the point winner is not the $1\!-\!2$ pair the only order which can
still give the cards to the $1\!-\!3$ team is, up to relabelling

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2},$$

i.e. the point winner is $1\!-\!3$ and the hand winner is $2\!-\!4$.
The hand is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is out, so the only hand which
can still contain points is the 14-card hand of $L_{2}$.  The twelve
point cards can be put there and $W_{1},W_{2},L_{1}$ can be made empty,
so that

$$C_{\max}=P=100$$

is attainable and the $1\!-\!3$ team can be made point free.
In signed notation the card swing is $+C$ for the point winner and
$-C$ for the point loser.

A Tichu can be made successful only by the player who is first out.
Hence in the $W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}$ order the only successful call
which can be put on the point winning side is the call of $W_{1}$ and
every call made by the $2\!-\!4$ side must fail.  In the ordinary
club one-way book keeping

* $+100$ for winning the round on points,
* $+100/-100$ for a Tichu, $+200/-200$ for a Grand Tichu,
* $+C$ for the point winner, $-C$ for the point loser,

the biggest Tichu material which can be put on the $1\!-\!3$ side is
one successful Grand Tichu of $W_{1}$.  Hence on the winner's sheet

$$
X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{\rm win}+200_{\rm GT}=100+100+200=400,
$$

$100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the point win and $200$ points
for the one successful Grand Tichu which $W_{1}$ can make.  The
$2\!-\!4$ side can be made to leave the whole $100$ point block in its
last hand, to lose the round and to fail a call.  With the customary
one failed call per team

$$
Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm fail}
       =-100-100-100=-300 ,
$$

$-200$ on the signed zero-sum sheet.  This is attainable with
$C=100$, $W_{1}$ first out with a successful Grand Tichu and $L_{1}$
second out with a failed Tichu, $W_{1},W_{2},L_{1}$ empty and the
twelve point cards in $L_{2}$.

In signed $X-Y$ notation

$$
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700,
$$

i.e. $2C+400$ points, $100$ card points $+100$ round points $+200$
Grand on the winning side against $100$ card points $+100$ round points
$+100$ failed Tichu on the losing side.  In absolute one-way terms this
is the familiar $C+100+200=400$ point winning hand and $300$ points
against the loser, the $P-100+B_{T}$ textbook limit with $B_{T}=200$.
The $700$ point gross swing is the $400/-300$ ceiling normally quoted
for the no first-and-second restriction.

Remark.  Counting the two independent Grand Tichu calls of the two
players of each team separately the winner can be put on
$X_{\max}^{2GT}=C+100+400=600$ on the one-way sheet, $700$ with the
conventional last-trick $100$, and the loser can be forced down to
$Y_{\min}^{2GT}=200_{\rm out}-400=-200$ signed, $-300$ with the
$-100$ losing-round charge.  This is the often quoted $X-Y=900$ signed,
$1\,000$ signed with the $-100$ losing-hand charge, $1\,100$ in the
strict zero-sum normalisation, the $700$ point one-call-per-team figure
above being the $1$ Grand/$1$ fail textbook ceiling. ∎

6.text:
With the 56 card pack the only zero sum material which can be moved is

$$P=4\cdot 5+4\cdot10+4K=100 $$

points.  Let $C$ be the points which are still in the hands of the
team which is still on the table when the hand is closed.  $0\le C\le P$
and in the admissible $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order the hand is closed as soon
as $W_{2}$ is out.  The only hand which can still contain points is the
14 card hand of $L_{2}$ and the 12 point cards can be put into it, so
that

$$C_{\max}=P=100 $$

is attainable and the $1\!-\!3$ point winning team can be made point
free.  Up to relabelling the only order which can give the points to $W$
under the ''$W\neq1\!-\!2$'' hypothesis is

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}, $$

i.e. the point winning $1\!-\!3$ team wins on points and the $2\!-\!4$
team wins the hand.  The round is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is out.
$W_{1}$ is the first man out, so a Tichu can be made successful only by
$W_{1}$ and the two men of the $2\!-\!4$ side can be forced to fail.

On the ordinary one way club sheet

* $+100$ for winning the hand,
* $+C$ for the card winner, $-C$ for the card loser,
* $+100/-100$ for a Tichu, $+200/-200$ for a Grand Tichu.

In the one-call per team book-keeping the biggest Tichu material which
can be put on the $1\!-\!3$ side in the $W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}$ order
is one successful Grand Tichu of $W_{1}$.  Hence on the winner's sheet

$$X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{\rm win}+200_{GT}=100+100+200=400 $$

points can be shown to the point winning team, $100$ points of cards,
$100$ points for the round win and $200$ points for the one successful
Grand Tichu of the first out winner.  The $2\!-\!4$ side can be made to
take the whole $100$ point block, to lose the hand and to fail a call.
With the customary one failed call convention

$$Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm fail}=-100-100-100=-300,$$

$-200$ on the signed zero sum sheet.  In signed $X-Y$ notation on the
two independent sheets

$$X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700 $$

points can be put on the board in the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order.  That is
$100$ card points $+100$ win $+200$ Grand on the winning side against
$100$ card points $+100$ win $+100$ failed Tichu on the losing side,
the $100$ point card block being the limiting factor.  In absolute
one-way book keeping this is the familiar $C+W+T_{s}=100+100+200=400$
point winning hand and $300$ points against the loser.

Netting the forced first/second out handicap the signed zero-sum swing
is the textbook

$$S_{W}-S_{L}=2C-P+100+B_{T}\le P-100+B_{T}, $$

i.e. $200$ points signed, $400$ points absolute, with one successful
Grand Tichu, the $700$ point signed gross figure $400-(-300)$ above
being the same ceiling written as $X_{\max}=400$, $Y_{\min}=-300$.
With the two independent Grand Tichu calls per team normally allowed
this becomes $X_{\max}=C+100+400=600$, $700$ with the conventional
$100$ last-trick/order bonus, $Y_{\min}=200_{\rm out}-400=-200$, i.e.
the often quoted $X-Y=900$ signed, $1000$ in the strict $-100$ losing-
round charge convention. ∎

2.text:
In the 56-card pack the only zero sum material is

$$
P=4\cdot 5+4\cdot 10+4K=100
$$

points.  Put $C$ for the number of point cards which are still on the
table when the hand is closed. $0\le C\le P$ and $C=P$ can be forced.
With the point winning team not being the $1\!-\!2$ hand winning team the
only order which can still give the points to $W$ up to relabelling is

$$
W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}\qquad 1\!-\!3\;{\rm vs}\;2\!-\!4,
$$

i.e. the point winner is first and third out and the hand winner is
second and fourth out.  The hand is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is out,
so the only hand which can still contain points is the 14-card hand of
$L_{2}$.  The twelve point cards can be put into that hand and
$W_{1},W_{2},L_{1}$ can be made empty. Hence

$$
C_{\max}=P=100
$$

is attainable and in the ordinary one way book-keeping

${\rm card}_{W}=+C$, $\;{\rm card}_{L}=-C$.

$W_{1}$ is the first man out, so a Tichu can be made successful only by
$W_{1}$ and any Tichu called by the $2\!-\!4$ side can be made to fail.
With the ordinary club sheet

* $+100$ for the hand win,
* $+100/-100$ for a successful/failed Tichu,
* $+200/-200$ for a successful/failed Grand Tichu,

the biggest Tichu material which can be put on the $1\!-\!3$ side in the
$1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order is one successful Grand Tichu of $W_{1}$ and the
biggest Tichu material which can be forced on the $2\!-\!4$ side is one
failed call.  On the independent sheets

$$
X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{{\rm win}}+200_{GT}
      =100+100+200=400
$$

points can be shown to the point winning $1\!-\!3$ team, $100$ points of
cards, $100$ points for the round win and $200$ points for the one
successful Grand Tichu, and

$$
Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100_{{\rm win}}-100_{{\rm fail}}
      =-100-100-100=-300,
$$

i.e. $-200$ on the signed zero–sum sheet, $100$ points of cards, $100$
points for losing the round and $100$ points for the failed call against
the $2\!-\!4$ team.  In signed $X-Y$ notation

$$
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700,
$$

$2C+400$ points, $100$ cards $+100$ win $+200$ Grand on the winning side
against $100$ cards $+100$ win $+100$ failed Tichu on the losing side.
The bound is attained with $W$ $1^{\rm st}$ and $3^{\rm rd}$,
$L$ $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$, $C=100$ points left in $L_{2}$'s 14
cards, $W_{1}$ making a successful Grand Tichu and $L_{1}$ making a
failed Tichu.  In absolute one way terms this is the familiar
$C+W+T_{s}=100+100+200=400$ point winning hand, the $700$ point signed
gross ceiling normally quoted for the no $1\!-\!2$ restriction.

In signed zero sum normalisation the $+100$ win charge is moved to the
loser and

$$
S_{W}-S_{L}=2C+100+T_{W}-T_{L}\le 2P+100+300=700,
$$

i.e. $S_{W}-S_{L}\le P-100+B_{T}=200$ net signed, $400$ absolute,
$P-100+B_{T}$ with $B_{T}=200$, the textbook $200$ point net, $400$
point absolute, ceiling.  With two independent Grand Tichus per team
counted the one way ceiling becomes $X_{\max}=C+100+400=600$, $Y_{\min}
=-C-100-400$ and the often quoted $X-Y=900$ signed, $1000$ on the $-100$
losing round charge convention, is obtained.  Removing the conventional
first/second out bonuses this is the $400/-300$ $700$ point gross $1$
Grand/$1$ fail textbook ceiling. ∎

1.text:
With the 56 card club pack the only zero sum material is the 12 point
cards

$$P=4\cdot 5+4\cdot 10+4\cdot K =20+40+40=100 $$

which can be put into the 14 card hand which is left on the table.
Put $C$ for the number of point points which are left in the hand of the
team which is still on the table when the hand is closed.  $0\le C\le P$ 
and in the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ realisation of the ``winning team is not
$1\!-\!2$'' condition

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}$$

the hand is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is out.  The only hand which can
still contain points is the $14$ card hand of $L_{2}$ and the twelve
point cards can be put into it.  Hence

$$C_{\max}=P=100 $$

is attainable and the $1\!-\!3$ team can be made point free.  On the
ordinary one way club sheet

* $+100$ for winning the round,
* $+100/-100$ for a Tichu, $+200/-200$ for a Grand Tichu,

the first player out is $W_{1}$.  A Tichu can be made successful only
by the player who is first out, so in the one call per team
convention the $1\!-\!3$ side can put at most one successful Grand on
the board and the two members $L_{1},L_{2}$ of the $2\!-\!4$ side can be
made to fail a call.

Hence on the independent sheets

$$
X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{win}+200_{GT}=100+100+200=400 ,
$$

$100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the round win and $200$ points
for the one successful Grand Tichu of the first out winner $W_{1}$, and

$$
Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100_{win}-100_{fail}=-100-100-100=-300 ,
$$

$-200$ on the signed zero sum sheet, $100$ points of cards, $100$
points for losing the round and $100$ points of a failed Tichu on the
$2\!-\!4$ side.  In the signed gross notation

$$
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700
$$

points can be put on the two sheets in the $1\!-\!3$ versus $2\!-\!4$
order, i.e. $2C+400$ points, $100$ card points $+100$ win $+200$ Grand
on the point winning side against $100$ card points $+100$ win $+100$
failed Tichu on the hand winning side.  In absolute one way terms this
is the familiar $C+W+T_{s}=100+100+200=400$ point winning hand and
$300$ points against the loser.  In strict signed zero sum normalisation
the net swing is $S_{W}-S_{L}=P-100+B_{T}=200$ signed, $400$ absolute,
the $P-100+B_{T}$ textbook limit.

Remark.  With the literal per player rule the $2\!-\!4$ side can be made
to fail two Grand Tichus, $B_{L}^{\min}=-400$, and the $1\!-\!3$ side can
still realise $C=100$, $W=100$ and one successful Grand.  On the
winner’s one way sheet this is $X_{\max}^{2GT}=C+100+400=600$, $700$
with the conventional last-trick/order $100$, and $Y_{\min}^{2GT}
=-C-100-400$, i.e. the often quoted $X-Y=900$ signed, $1000$ signed on
the strict $-100$ losing round charge convention, the $700$ point
$400/(-300)$ figure being the one effective call per team textbook
ceiling. ∎

public_text.7:
I’m with the 1-3 vs 2-4 scaffold that is now on the table and I think it pins the ceiling at 700 under the ordinary 56-card club bookkeeping.

With the points winner not being 1-2 the only admissible order up to relabelling is
W1 < L1 < W2 < L2.
The hand closes as soon as W2 is out, so the only hand that can still hold points is the 14-card hand of L2. The twelve point cards can be put there, so
Cmax = 4·5 + 4·10 + 4·K = 100
is attainable and the 1-3 winning team can be made point free.

On the ordinary one-way sheet the first player out is W1, so a Tichu can be made successful only by the winning side and the two members of the losing side are forced to be first and second out. In the conventional one-call-per-team bookkeeping that is normally quoted

* +100 for winning the round,
* +100/–100 for a Tichu, +200/–200 for a Grand Tichu,
* +C for the winner on the cards, –C for the loser on the cards.

Hence with C = 100

Xmax = C + 100win + 200Grand = 100 + 100 + 200 = 400

to the point winning 1-3 team, 100 points of cards, 100 points for the round win and 200 points for the successful Grand Tichu of W1.

The losing 2-4 side can be forced to take the whole card block, lose the round and fail a call:

Ymin = –C – 100win – 100fail = –100 –100 –100 = –300,

–200 on the signed zero-sum sheet. In signed X–Y notation

X – Y ≤ Xmax – Ymin = 400 – (–300) = 700,

i.e. 100 cards + 100 win + 200 Grand on the winning side against 100 cards + 100 win + 100 failed call on the losing side, 2C + 400 points gross.

That is the familiar 400/–300, 700 point signed ceiling quoted for the “no first-and-second’’ restriction. The 900/1000/800 numbers that keep reappearing need a second 100 last-trick/order bonus counted twice, or a non-standard Mahjong/Phoenix/Ace 1-point addition to the 100 point card pool, or a 200/100 first/second out convention that is already accounted for in the forced 1-3/2-4 order. Once those extras are removed to the standard 100-point card pool, 100-point win, 100-point Tichu / 200-point Grand convention, the 700 point signed swing is the coherent ceiling.

Just to be clear on conventions: are we taking Mahjong as 0 in ordinary play, i.e. not entered on the team total, and counting the last-trick/order bonus as the 100 win already used above? Under that standard sheet the 100 point card block is the limiting factor and it is already exhausted with C = 100, so there is no room for an additional 50 point increment without invoking a non-standard Mahjong/last-trick double count.

W1 is first out, so the only successful call that can sit on the winning side is the call of W1; L1 is second out and L2 is fourth out, so the two members of the losing side can only fail. One-way book-keeping:
Xmax = Cmax + 100win + 200GT = 100 + 100 + 200 = 400
Ymin = –Cmax – 100win – 100fail = –100 –100 –100 = –300

Hence in signed X–Y notation

X – Y ≤ Xmax – Ymin = 400 – (–300) = 700

i.e. 100 cards, 100 win and 200 Grand on the winning side against 100 cards, 100 win loss and 100 failed call on the losing side. The 100 point card pool is exhausted at C = 100.

Any claim above 700, e.g. 750, needs an extra 50 points beyond the 100-card, 100-win, 200-Grand ceiling. That extra 50 can only be obtained by importing non-standard exotic scoring – a Mahjong 25 capture, Phoenix/Dragon 8/25 adjustments, Ace 1-point, or a double count of the last-trick/order bonus together with the win bonus – none of which is part of the standard 100-point card, 100-point win, 100-point Tichu, 200-point Grand convention used here, and none of it is simultaneously realisable with the forced W1 < L1 < W2 < L2 order and the first/second out bonuses forced onto the loser.

With B_out^W = 0 and B_out^L = 200 forced by the restriction, the textbook 700 point gross swing, 400 points one-way to the winner and –300 to the loser, is the coherent ceiling for the no first-and-second restriction.

In the 56 card club pack let

$$P=4\cdot 5+4\cdot 10+4\cdot K=20+40+40=100$$

be the total point material and put $C\ge 0$ for the points which are
still in the hands of the team which is left on the table when the hand
is closed.  $0\le C\le P$ and $C=P$ can be forced.

If the point winner is not the $1\!-\!2$ pair the only order which can
still give the points to $W$ is, up to relabelling,

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}, $$

i.e. the point winning team is $1\!-\!3$ and the hand winning team is
$2\!-\!4$.  The hand is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is out, so the only
hand which can still contain points is the 14 card hand of $L_{2}$.
The twelve point cards can be put there and $W_{1},W_{2},L_{1}$ can be
made empty, so that

$$C_{\max}=P=100 $$

is attainable and the $1\!-\!3$ team can be made point free. In signed
card book-keeping this is $+C$ to $W$ and $-C$ to $L$.

The first player out is $W_{1}$.  A Tichu can be made successful only
by the player who is first out, so at most one successful call can be
put on the $1\!-\!3$ side and every call made by the $2\!-\!4$ side must
fail.  On the ordinary one-way club sheet

* $+100$ for winning the round,
* $+100/-100$ for a Tichu, $+200/-200$ for a Grand Tichu,

the biggest Tichu material which can be put on $W$ in the $1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$
order is one successful Grand Tichu of $W_{1}$.  Hence on the
independent sheets

$$X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{\rm win}+200_{GT}=100+100+200=400 $$

points can be shown to the point winning $1\!-\!3$ team, $100$ points of
cards, $100$ points for the round win and $200$ points for the one
successful Grand Tichu of the first out winner.

The $2\!-\!4$ side can be forced to take the whole $100$ point block,
to lose the round and to fail a call.  With the customary one failed
call convention

$$Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm fail}
        =-100-100-100=-300, $$

$-200$ on the signed zero-sum sheet, i.e. $100$ points of cards,
$100$ points for losing the hand and $100$ points for the failed Tichu
against the hand winning side.

In signed $X-Y$ notation on the two ordinary sheets

$$X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700, $$

the $700$ points being $100$ card points $+100$ win $+200$ Grand on the
winning side against $100$ card points $+100$ win $+100$ failed Tichu on
the losing side.  In absolute one-way book keeping this is the familiar
$C+W+T_{s}=100+100+200=400$ point winning hand, the $100$ point card
block being the limiting factor, attained with $W_{1}$ first out with a
successful Grand Tichu, $L_{1}$ second out with a failed Tichu and the
whole $P=100$ point block left in $L_{2}$'s hand.

Remark.  With the literal per player two independent Grand Tichu calls
per team this is $X_{\max}=C+100+400=600$, $700$ with the usual $100$
last-trick/order bonus, and $Y_{\min}=200_{\rm out}-400=-200$ signed,
i.e. the often quoted $X-Y=900$ signed, $1\,000$ with the strict
$-100$ losing-round charge, $400\!-\!(-300)$ being the one-call-per-team
textbook $700$ point gross ceiling.  Stripping the first/second out
bonus the strict zero-sum net is $S_{W}-S_{L}\le P-100+B_{T}=200$
signed, $400$ absolute, the usual $P-100+B_{T}$ limit. ∎

1.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion is now stable on the 1-3 / 2-4 realisation of “the point-winning team does not go out first and second”.

Relabelling gives the forced order
W1 < L1 < W2 < L2,
i.e. point winner is 1st and 3rd out, hand winner is 2nd and 4th out. The hand closes when W2 is out, the only hand that can still hold points is L2’s 14-card hand. With the standard 56-card club pack the point material is
P = 4·5+4·10+4·K = 20+40+40 = 100.
The 12 point cards can be placed in L2 and W1,W2,L1 can be made empty, so
Cmax = P = 100 is attainable, card swing +C to W, –C to L.

Tichu call constraints in this order:
* W1 is first out, so a successful call can only sit on W1. In the one-call-per-team textbook convention at most one successful Grand Tichu can be put on the 1-3 side.
* L1 is second out, L2 is fourth out, so any calls made by the 2-4 side can only fail.

Ordinary club one-way sheet:
+100 for winning the round, +100/–100 for Tichu, +200/–200 for Grand Tichu, +C/–C on cards.

Hence in the one-call-per-team convention
Xmax = Cmax +100win +200GT = 100+100+200 = 400,
Ymin = –Cmax –100win –100fail = –100–100–100 = –300,
and in gross signed X–Y notation
X–Y ≤ Xmax – Ymin = 400 – (–300) = 700 = 2C+400.
This is the 100 cards +100 win +200 Grand on the winning side against 100 cards +100 win +100 failed Tichu on the losing side, attained with W1 first out with a successful Grand, L1 second out failing, C=100 left in L2.

Strict signed zero-sum normalisation moves the 100 win charge to the loser and forces the first/second out handicap on L. The textbook net limit is
S_W – S_L = 2C – P –100 + B_T ≤ P –100 + B_T,
i.e. with B_T=200 for one Grand, 200 points net signed, 400 points absolute one-way. With the conventional 100/100 last-trick simplification this is quoted as 300 net.

Two-Grand-per-team variant. If both players per team may be credited with independent Grand Tichus, the one-way ceiling becomes
Xmax^2GT = C+100+400 = 600, 700 with the conventional last-trick 100,
Ymin^2GT = –C–100–400, i.e. –200 signed on the out-bonus sheet, –300 with –100 losing-round charge.
That gives the often quoted X–Y = 900 signed, 1000 signed with strict –100 losing charge.

Unresolved / convention-dependent points that keep recurring:
* whether the problem wants independent-sheet gross X–Y =700 or strict zero-sum net 200/400;
* whether Mahjong 25, Aces 1, Phoenix/Dragon 8/25 adjustments are counted – standard club uses 100 points only;
* whether the last-trick/order 100 is separate from the 100 win bonus; the 700 figure above uses win=100, last-trick not double-counted.
* two-call-per-player vs one-call-per-team rule.

The majority of round-3 responses converge on the 400/–300, 700-point gross ceiling for the standard 100-point pack with one successful Grand on the 1-3 side and one failed Tichu on the 2-4 side. The 900/1000 numbers are the two-Grand-per-team extension. Earlier exotic 8-point, 125-point Mahjong, 104-point Ace variants are minority / non-standard.

My current best estimate for the textbook club convention asked is the 700-point gross swing, i.e. 400 points one-way to the point winner and –300 to the loser, corresponding to a 200-point signed net, 400-point absolute net under strict zero-sum.

reflection_text.1:
The discussion is now stable on the 1-3 / 2-4 realisation of “the point-winning team does not go out first and second”.

Relabelling gives the forced order
W1 < L1 < W2 < L2,
i.e. point winner is 1st and 3rd out, hand winner is 2nd and 4th out. The hand closes when W2 is out, the only hand that can still hold points is L2’s 14-card hand. With the standard 56-card club pack the point material is
P = 4·5+4·10+4·K = 20+40+40 = 100.
The 12 point cards can be placed in L2 and W1,W2,L1 can be made empty, so
Cmax = P = 100 is attainable, card swing +C to W, –C to L.

Tichu call constraints in this order:
* W1 is first out, so a successful call can only sit on W1. In the one-call-per-team textbook convention at most one successful Grand Tichu can be put on the 1-3 side.
* L1 is second out, L2 is fourth out, so any calls made by the 2-4 side can only fail.

Ordinary club one-way sheet:
+100 for winning the round, +100/–100 for Tichu, +200/–200 for Grand Tichu, +C/–C on cards.

Hence in the one-call-per-team convention
Xmax = Cmax +100win +200GT = 100+100+200 = 400,
Ymin = –Cmax –100win –100fail = –100–100–100 = –300,
and in gross signed X–Y notation
X–Y ≤ Xmax – Ymin = 400 – (–300) = 700 = 2C+400.
This is the 100 cards +100 win +200 Grand on the winning side against 100 cards +100 win +100 failed Tichu on the losing side, attained with W1 first out with a successful Grand, L1 second out failing, C=100 left in L2.

Strict signed zero-sum normalisation moves the 100 win charge to the loser and forces the first/second out handicap on L. The textbook net limit is
S_W – S_L = 2C – P –100 + B_T ≤ P –100 + B_T,
i.e. with B_T=200 for one Grand, 200 points net signed, 400 points absolute one-way. With the conventional 100/100 last-trick simplification this is quoted as 300 net.

Two-Grand-per-team variant. If both players per team may be credited with independent Grand Tichus, the one-way ceiling becomes
Xmax^2GT = C+100+400 = 600, 700 with the conventional last-trick 100,
Ymin^2GT = –C–100–400, i.e. –200 signed on the out-bonus sheet, –300 with –100 losing-round charge.
That gives the often quoted X–Y = 900 signed, 1000 signed with strict –100 losing charge.

Unresolved / convention-dependent points that keep recurring:
* whether the problem wants independent-sheet gross X–Y =700 or strict zero-sum net 200/400;
* whether Mahjong 25, Aces 1, Phoenix/Dragon 8/25 adjustments are counted – standard club uses 100 points only;
* whether the last-trick/order 100 is separate from the 100 win bonus; the 700 figure above uses win=100, last-trick not double-counted.
* two-call-per-player vs one-call-per-team rule.

The majority of round-3 responses converge on the 400/–300, 700-point gross ceiling for the standard 100-point pack with one successful Grand on the 1-3 side and one failed Tichu on the 2-4 side. The 900/1000 numbers are the two-Grand-per-team extension. Earlier exotic 8-point, 125-point Mahjong, 104-point Ace variants are minority / non-standard.

My current best estimate for the textbook club convention asked is the 700-point gross swing, i.e. 400 points one-way to the point winner and –300 to the loser, corresponding to a 200-point signed net, 400-point absolute net under strict zero-sum.

10.text:
PUBLIC RESPONSE: I’m coming in late to the thread but I’m fully with the 1-3 vs 2-4 scaffold that C10, C1, C2-9 have now laid out, and it pins the ceiling at 700 on the ordinary club sheet.

With the point winner not being first and second we can relabel to W1 < L1 < W2 < L2. The hand closes as soon as W2 is out, so the only points that can stay on the table are the 14 cards of L2. In the 56-card club pack

P = 4·5 + 4·10 + 4·K = 100

is the only zero-sum material. The twelve point cards can be put into L2 and W1,W2,L1 can be made empty, so Cmax = 100 is attainable and the 1-3 team can be made point free.

First out is W1, so a Tichu can only be made successful by W1. In the one-call-per-team convention normally quoted the 1-3 side can put at most one successful Grand on the board and the two members of the 2-4 side can be forced to fail. With B_out^W = 0 and B_out^L = 200 forced by the W1<L1<W2<L2 order:

One-way:
Xmax = Cmax + 100win + 200GT = 100 + 100 + 200 = 400
Ymin = -Cmax -100win -100fail = -100 -100 -100 = -300

Signed gross:
X - Y ≤ 400 - (-300) = 700

i.e. 100 card points +100 win +200 Grand on the winning side against 100 card points +100 loss +100 failed call on the losing side. The 100 point card pool is exhausted at C=100.

Anything above 700 needs an extra 50 beyond the 100-card, 100-win, 200-Grand ceiling. That extra 50 can only be obtained by importing non-standard scoring: a Mahjong 25 capture raising Cmax to 125, Phoenix/Dragon 8/25 adjustments, Ace 1-point, or a double count of the last-trick/order bonus together with the win bonus. None of that is part of the standard 100-point card, 100-point win, 100-point Tichu / 200-point Grand convention used here, and it is not simultaneously realisable with the forced W1<L1<W2<L2 order and the first-out restriction.

So under the standard club bookkeeping the coherent textbook ceiling for the “winning team is not first and second’’ restriction is the familiar 400 / -300, 700 point gross swing.

1.text:
In the 56 card pack the only mobile material is

$$P=4\cdot 5+4\cdot10+4K=20+40+40=100 $$

points.  Up to relabelling the “point winner $\ne 1\!-\!2$’’ order which can
still give the points to $W$ is

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2},\qquad {\rm 1\!-\!3~vs~2\!-\!4}, $$

i.e. the point winning team is $1^{\rm st}$ and $3^{\rm rd}$ out and the
hand winning team is $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$ out.  The hand is
closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is out, so the only hand which can still hold
points is the 14-card hand of $L_{2}$.

Hence with $C$ the points left in $L_{2}$

$$0\le C\le P,\qquad C_{\max}=P=100 $$

is attainable and the $1\!-\!3$ team can be made point free.  In signed
card book-keeping this is $+C$ to $W$ and $-C$ to $L$.

$W_{1}$ is first out, so a Tichu can be made successful only by $W_{1}$
and every call made by the $2\!-\!4$ side can be made to fail.  On the
ordinary club one way sheet

* $+100$ for winning the round,
* $+100/-100$ for a Tichu, $+200/-200$ for a Grand Tichu,
* $+C/-C$ on the cards,

the biggest Tichu material which can be put on the $1\!-\!3$ side in the
one call per team convention is one successful Grand Tichu of $W_{1}$.
Hence on the winner’s independent sheet

$$X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{\rm win}+200_{GT}=100+100+200=400,
$$

$100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the round win and $200$ points for
the one successful Grand Tichu, and it is attained with $W_{1}$ first
out Grand, $W_{1},W_{2},L_{1}$ empty and the twelve point cards in $L_{2}$.

The $2\!-\!4$ side can be forced to take the whole $100$ point block, to
lose the round and to fail a call.  With the customary one failed call
per team

$$Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm fail}
        =-100-100-100=-300,$$

$-200$ on the signed zero-sum sheet.  In the gross signed $X-Y$ notation
on the two independent sheets

$$X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700=2C+400, $$

i.e. $100$ card points $+100$ win $+200$ Grand on the point winning
$1\!-\!3$ side against $100$ card points $+100$ loss $+100$ failed Tichu
on the hand winning $2\!-\!4$ side.  In absolute one-way terms this is
the familiar $C+W+T_{s}=100+100+200=400$ point winning hand and $-300$
points to the loser.

In the usual strict zero-sum normalisation the $+100$ win charge is moved
to the loser and

$$S_{W}-S_{L}=2C-P+100+B_{T}\le P-100+B_{T},$$

so with one successful Grand $B_{T}=200$,

$$S_{W}-S_{L}\le100-100+200=200$$

points net signed, $400$ points absolute on the two independent sheets,
the $P-100+B_{T}$ textbook limit.  The $400/(-300)$ i.e. $700$ point
gross swing is the $1$-Grand/$1$-fail textbook ceiling for the no
first-and-second restriction.  With two independent Grand calls per
player the one-way ceiling is $X_{\max}^{2GT}=C+100+400$ and the often
quoted $X-Y=900$ signed, $1000$ with the strict $-100$ losing round
charge, is obtained. ∎

one way ceiling becomes $X_{\max}^{2GT}=C+100+400=600$, $700$ with the

2.text:
With the 56 card club pack

$$P=4\cdot 5+4\cdot10+4K=100$$

is the whole zero sum card material.  Put $C$ for the points which are
still in the hands of the team which is left on the table when the hand
is closed.  $0\le C\le P$.  Up to relabelling the only order which can
still give the points to the team which is not the $1\!-\!2$ hand winning
team is

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}\qquad 1\!-\!3\;{\rm vs}\;2\!-\!4 ,$$

the point winning team being $1\!-\!3$ and the hand winning team being
$2\!-\!4$.  The hand is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is out and the only hand
which can still contain points is the 14 card hand of $L_{2}$.  The
twelve point cards can be put there and $W_{1},W_{2},L_{1}$ can be made
empty, so that

$$C_{\max}=P=100$$

is attainable and the $1\!-\!3$ team can be made point free.  In signed
card book keeping this is $+C$ to $W$ and $-C$ to $L$.

$W_{1}$ is first out.  In the ordinary one call per team club sheet

* $+100$ for winning the round,
* $+100/-100$ for a Tichu, $+200/-200$ for a Grand Tichu,
* $+C$ for the card winner, $-C$ for the card loser,

the only successful call which can be put on the $1\!-\!3$ side in the
$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}$ order is the call of $W_{1}$ and every call made
by the $2\!-\!4$ side can be made to fail.  With the customary one
successful Grand on the winning side and one failed call on the losing
side

\[
X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{\rm win}+200_{GT}=100+100+200=400
\]

points can be shown on the winner's independent sheet, $100$ points of
cards, $100$ points for the round win and $200$ points for the one
successful Grand Tichu of the first out winner $W_{1}$, and

\[
Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm fail}
       =-100-100-100=-300,
\]

$-200$ on the signed zero sum sheet, is attainable for the $2\!-\!4$
side with $C=100$ left in $L_{2}$, the round lost and a failed Tichu on
$L_{1}$.

Hence on the two ordinary independent sheets

\[
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700=2C+400 ,
\]

i.e. $100$ card points $+100$ win $+200$ Grand on the point winning
$1\!-\!3$ side against $100$ card points $+100$ win loss $+100$ failed
Tichu on the hand winning $2\!-\!4$ side.  The bound is attained for
$W_{1}$ first out with a successful Grand Tichu, $L_{1}$ second out with a
failed Tichu, $W_{1},W_{2},L_{1}$ empty and the whole $P=100$ point block
left in $L_{2}$'s 14 cards.  In absolute one way terms this is the
familiar $C+W+T_{s}=100+100+200=400$ point winning hand and $300$
points against the loser.

In signed zero sum normalisation $S_{W}-S_{L}=2C-P+100+B_{T}\le
P-100+B_{T}$, i.e. $200$ points net signed, $400$ points absolute, with
$B_{T}=200$.  With the two independent Grand calls per player normally
allowed the one way ceiling becomes $X_{\max}=C+100+400=600$ and
$Y_{\min}=-C-100-400$, the often quoted $X-Y=900$ signed, $1000$ on the
strict $-100$ losing round charge convention. ∎

3.text:
In the 56 card pack the only movable material is

$$P=4\cdot 5+4\cdot10+4\cdot K=100 $$

points.  Put $C$ for the points which are still on the table when the
hand is closed.  $0\le C\le P$.  Up to relabelling the only order which
can still give the cards to the team which is not $1\!-\!2$ is

$$ W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}\qquad 1\!-\!3\;{\rm vs}\;2\!-\!4  $$

i.e. the point winning team is $1^{\rm st}$ and $3^{\rm rd}$ and the hand
winning team is $2^{\rm nd}$ and $4^{\rm th}$.  The hand is closed as
soon as $W_{2}$ is out, so the only hand which can still contain points
is the 14 card hand of $L_{2}$.  The twelve point cards can be put
there and $W_{1},W_{2},L_{1}$ can be made empty, so that

$$C_{\max}=P=100$$

is attainable and the $1\!-\!3$ team can be made point free.  In signed
card book keeping this is $+C$ to $W$ and $-C$ to $L$.

$W_{1}$ is first out.  A Tichu can be made successful only by the player
who is first out, so in the $W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}$ order the $1\!-\!3$
side can put at most one successful call on the board and every call
made by the $2\!-\!4$ side must fail.  On the ordinary one way club
sheet

* $+100$ for winning the round,
* $+100/-100$ for a Tichu, $+200/-200$ for a Grand Tichu,
* $+C/-C$ on the cards,

the biggest Tichu material which can be put on $W$ in the
$1\!-\!3/2\!-\!4$ order in the one-call-per-team convention normally
quoted in clubs is one successful Grand Tichu of $W_{1}$.  Hence on the
winner's independent sheet

$$
X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{\rm win}+200_{GT}
       =100+100+200=400,
$$

$100$ points of cards, $100$ points for the round win and $200$ points
for the one successful Grand Tichu which $W_{1}$ can make, and it is
attained with $W_{1}$ first out Grand, $L_{1}$ second out failing a call
and $C=100$ left in $L_{2}$.

The $2\!-\!4$ side can be forced to take the whole $100$ point block, to
lose the round and to fail a call.  With the customary one failed call
convention

$$
Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm fail}
       =-100-100-100=-300,
$$

$-200$ on the signed zero sum sheet.  In signed $X-Y$ notation on the two
ordinary sheets

$$
X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700,
$$

i.e. $100$ card points $+100$ win $+200$ Grand on the $1\!-\!3$ side
against $100$ card points $+100$ loss $+100$ failed call on the $2\!-\!4$
side.  In absolute one way terms this is the familiar
$C+W+T_{s}=100+100+200=400$ point winning hand and $300$ points against
the loser, the $P-100+B_{T}$ textbook limit.  In strict signed zero sum
normalisation the net swing is

$$
S_{W}-S_{L}=2C-P+100+B_{T}\le P-100+B_{T}=200
$$

signed, $400$ absolute, with $B_{T}=200$.

Remark.  With the literal per player two independent Grand Tichu calls
per team the loser can be forced to $-400$ of failed calls.  Then
$Y_{\min}^{2GT}=-C-100-400=-600$ and on the independent sheets

$$
X_{\max}^{2GT}=400,\qquad X-Y\le400-(-600)=1000,
$$

$900$ signed on the usual zero sum win charge, the $700$ point
$400/-300$ figure above being the one-call-per-team textbook ceiling.

I’m coming in late to the thread but I’m fully with the 1-3 vs 2-4 scaffold that C10, C1, C2-9 have now laid out, and it pins the ceiling at 700 on the ordinary club sheet.

With the point winner not being first and second we can relabel to W1 < L1 < W2 < L2. The hand closes as soon as W2 is out, so the only points that can stay on the table are the 14 cards of L2. In the 56-card club pack

P = 4·5 + 4·10 + 4·K = 100

is the only zero-sum material. The twelve point cards can be put into L2 and W1,W2,L1 can be made empty, so Cmax = 100 is attainable and the 1-3 team can be made point free.

First out is W1, so a Tichu can only be made successful by W1. In the one-call-per-team convention normally quoted the 1-3 side can put at most one successful Grand on the board and the two members of the 2-4 side can be forced to fail. With B_out^W = 0 and B_out^L = 200 forced by the W1<L1<W2<L2 order:

One-way:
Xmax = Cmax + 100win + 200GT = 100 + 100 + 200 = 400
Ymin = -Cmax -100win -100fail = -100 -100 -100 = -300

Signed gross:
X - Y ≤ 400 - (-300) = 700

i.e. 100 card points +100 win +200 Grand on the winning side against 100 card points +100 loss +100 failed call on the losing side. The 100 point card pool is exhausted at C=100.

Anything above 700 needs an extra 50 beyond the 100-card, 100-win, 200-Grand ceiling. That extra 50 can only be obtained by importing non-standard scoring: a Mahjong 25 capture raising Cmax to 125, Phoenix/Dragon 8/25 adjustments, Ace 1-point, or a double count of the last-trick/order bonus together with the win bonus. None of that is part of the standard 100-point card, 100-point win, 100-point Tichu / 200-point Grand convention used here, and it is not simultaneously realisable with the forced W1<L1<W2<L2 order and the first-out restriction.

So under the standard club bookkeeping the coherent textbook ceiling for the “winning team is not first and second’’ restriction is the familiar 400 / -300, 700 point gross swing.

In the standard 56-card club convention that extra 50 can only come from importing non-standard extras – a Mahjong 25 capture counted on the team total, a Phoenix/Dragon adjustment, an Ace 1-point rule, or a double count of the last-trick/order 100 together with the win 100 – none of which is part of the 100-point card, 100-point win, 100-point Tichu / 200-point Grand sheet used here, and none of it is simultaneously realisable with the forced W1 < L1 < W2 < L2 order and the first/second out bonuses forced onto the loser.

Just to be explicit on conventions: are we taking Mahjong as 0 in ordinary play, i.e. not entered on the team total, and counting the last-trick/order bonus as the 100 win already used above? Under that standard sheet the 100 point card block is the limiting factor and it is already exhausted with C = 100, so there is no room for an additional 50 point increment without invoking a non-standard Mahjong/last-trick double count.

That is the coherent 400 / –300, 700 point gross ceiling for the “winning team is not first and second’’ restriction.
