In the 56-card club pack the only zero-sum material is

$$P=4\cdot5+4\cdot10+4K=100$$

points.  Write $C$ for the points which are still on the table when the
hand is closed, $0\le C\le P$.  Up to relabelling the only finishing
order which can give the points to a team which is not the $1\!-\!2$
hand winning team and which can still make that team point free is

$$W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2},\qquad 1\!-\!3\;{\rm vs}\;2\!-\!4, $$

the point winning team being $1\!-\!3$ and the hand winning team
$2\!-\!4$.  The hand is closed as soon as $W_{2}$ is out, so the only
hand which can still contain points is the 14-card hand of $L_{2}$.
The twelve point cards can be put there and $W_{1},W_{2},L_{1}$ can be
made empty, so that

$$C_{\max}=P=100 $$

is attainable and the $1\!-\!3$ team can be made point free.  In signed
card book-keeping this is $+C$ to $W$ and $-C$ to $L$.

$W_{1}$ is the first man out.  A Tichu can be made successful only by
the player who is first out, so in the $W_{1}<L_{1}<W_{2}<L_{2}$ order
the only successful call which can sit on the $1\!-\!3$ side is the
call of $W_{1}$ and every call made by the $2\!-\!4$ side can be made
to fail.  On the ordinary one-way club sheet

* $+100$ for winning the round,
* $+100/-100$ for a Tichu, $+200/-200$ for a Grand Tichu,
* $+C$ to the point winner, $-C$ to the point loser,

with the usual one-call-per-team book-keeping the biggest Tichu
material which can be put on $W$ is one successful Grand Tichu of
$W_{1}$.

Hence on the independent sheets

$$X_{\max}=C_{\max}+100_{\rm win}+200_{GT}=100+100+200=400
$$

points can be shown to the point winning $1\!-\!3$ team, $100$ points
of cards, $100$ points for the round win and $200$ points for the one
successful Grand Tichu of the first out winner $W_{1}$.

The $2\!-\!4$ side can be forced to take the whole $100$ point block,
to lose the round and to fail a call.  With the customary one failed
call convention

$$Y_{\min}=-C_{\max}-100_{\rm win}-100_{\rm fail}
       =-100-100-100=-300,
$$

$-200$ on the signed zero-sum sheet, $100$ points of cards, $100$ points
for losing the round and $100$ points for the failed Tichu against the
hand winning side.  The bound is attained with $W_{1}$ first out with a
successful Grand Tichu, $L_{1}$ second out with a failed Tichu,
$W_{1},W_{2},L_{1}$ empty and the twelve point cards in $L_{2}$.

In signed $X-Y$ gross notation on the two ordinary sheets

$$X-Y\le X_{\max}-Y_{\min}=400-(-300)=700,
$$

i.e. $2C+400$ points, $100$ card points $+100$ win $+200$ Grand on the
winning side against $100$ card points $+100$ win $+100$ failed Tichu on
the losing side.  In absolute one-way terms this is the familiar
$C+W+T_{s}=100+100+200=400$ point winning hand and $300$ points
against the loser.

In the usual signed zero-sum normalisation the $+100$ win charge is
moved to the loser and

$$S_{W}-S_{L}=2C+100+T_{W}-T_{L}\le P-100+B_{T}, $$

i.e. $200$ points net signed, $400$ points absolute, with one
successful Grand Tichu, the $700$ point gross $400-(-300)$ figure being
the same ceiling written as $X_{\max}=400$, $Y_{\min}=-300$.  With two
independent Grand calls per team counted separately the one-way
ceiling becomes $X_{\max}^{2GT}=C+100+400=600$ and the often quoted
$X-Y=900$ signed, $1000$ with the strict $-100$ losing-round charge,
is obtained. ∎

3.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The discussion has now converged on the 1-3 vs 2-4 scaffold with the standard 56-card club pack.

Point material: P = 4·5 + 4·10 + 4·K = 100 points. Up to relabelling the only admissible closing order that can still give the points to the non-1-2 team is W1 < L1 < W2 < L2, i.e. the point winning team is 1st-3rd and the hand winning team is 2nd-4th. The hand closes as soon as W2 is out, so the only hand that can still hold points is L2’s 14-card hand. The twelve point cards can be placed there, so Cmax = P = 100 is attainable and the 1-3 team can be made point free. Card bookkeeping in signed form is +C to W, –C to L.

W1 is first out, so a Tichu can be successful only by W1 and any call made by the 2-4 side can be forced to fail. Under the ordinary club one-call-per-team sheet:
+100 for winning the round, +100/–100 Tichu, +200/–200 Grand Tichu, +C/–C cards.
First/second out bonuses are forced onto the loser.

One-call-per-team textbook ceiling now universally quoted in round 4:
Xmax = Cmax +100 win +200 Grand = 100+100+200 = 400
Ymin = –Cmax –100 win –100 fail = –100–100–100 = –300  [–200 on strict signed zero-sum sheet]
Gross signed X–Y ≤ 400 – (–300) = 700 = 2C + 400.

In strict signed zero-sum normalisation S_W – S_L = 2C – P +100 + B_T ≤ P –100 + B_T, with B_T = 200 → ≤200 signed net, 400 absolute one-way, the P–100+B_T textbook limit.

Variations still alive from earlier rounds:
* Literal per-player two independent Grand calls per team: Xmax² = C+100+400 =600, Ymin² = –C–100–400 = –600, giving X–Y = 900 signed, 1000 with strict –100 losing-round charge.
* Signed zero-sum net after removing double counting of win/out: S_W–S_L = 2C – P +100 + B_T – B_out, with C=100, B_T=200, B_out^L=200 → ≤200 net signed.
* Non-standard point variants: Mahjong 25 / Phoenix / Ace 1 raising Cmax to 102-125 etc., e.g. 125-point pack → 425 one-way, 850 signed gross, as in earlier Colleagues 8,9. Those are not part of the standard 100-point club convention used here.

Unresolved questions that keep recurring:
Signed vs absolute/one-way bookkeeping, whether Y is allowed negative, whether first/second out bonuses are scored separately from the win bonus, whether two Grand Tichus per team are counted, and the Mahjong/Phoenix/Ace scoring conventions. Current club-standard consensus in round 4 remains the 700-point signed gross ceiling, 400 one-way to the winner and –300 to the loser, with 200 net signed / 400 absolute zero-sum as the net form.

4.text:
PRIVATE REFLECTION: The 56-card club pack is the anchor. Point material is 4·5+4·10+4·K = 100 pts, zero-sum. With winning team not 1-2 the only realisable point-winning order up to relabelling is W1<L1<W2<L2, i.e. 1-3 vs 2-4. The hand closes on W2, so the only hand that can still hold points is the 14-card hand of L2. The twelve point cards can be placed there, W1,W2,L1 can be made empty, so Cmax =100 is attainable and the 1-3 team can be made point-free. Card swing is +C to the point winner, –C to the point loser.

First out is W1, second out is L1. A Tichu/Grand Tichu can be successful only by the first-out player, so in the 1-3/2-4 order at most one successful call can sit on the 1-3 side and the 2-4 side can only fail. On the ordinary one-way club sheet
* +100 for winning the round, –100 for losing it,
* +100/–100 for Tichu, +200/–200 for Grand Tichu,
* cards +C/–C.

With one call per team convention normally quoted:
Xmax = Cmax +100 win +200 GT = 100+100+200 =400
Ymin = –Cmax –100 win –100 fail = –100–100–100 = –300, –200 on the signed zero-sum sheet.
Hence on independent sheets X–Y ≤400–(–300)=700, i.e. 100 cards +100 win +200 Grand on the winner against 100 cards +100 win +100 failed Tichu on the loser. In strict signed zero-sum the 100 win is counted once, giving S_W–S_L =2C–P–100 +B_T ≤P–100+B_T =200 signed, 400 absolute with one Grand. This is the 400/–300, 700-point gross ceiling that colleagues 1,10,2,3,4,5,6,7,8,9 now converge on in round 4.

Disagreements/variants still present:
* Two independent Grand Tichus per player allowed: winner can still only succeed with W1, so Xmax =C+100+200=400 on the one-call-per-team sheet, but with literal per-player rule loser can be forced to fail two Grands, B_Lmin =–400, and winner can be shown C+100+400=600, 700 with conventional last-trick/order 100 counted. That gives often quoted Xmax=700, Ymin=–200 → X–Y=900 on independent sheets, 1000 with strict –100 losing-round charge. Colleagues 5,10,7,8 note this.
* First/second out bonuses: 200/100 convention vs 100/100 simplification vs removal. With 200/100 forced on loser net becomes familiar P–100+B_T limit.
* Exotic scoring: Mahjong 25 → Cmax=125 → Smax=125+100+200=425, signed 850; Ace 1-pt → P0=104, 14-heaviest=102 → Xmax=302, Ymin=–302, X–Y=604; special-card only 8-pt etc. These are non-standard.

Current working model remains ordinary 100-point card, 100-win, 200-Grand, 1-3 vs 2-4 convention: 700-point signed gross ceiling, 400 one-way to winner, –300 to loser. The 900/1000 numbers are two-failed-Grand per team extension; 200-point signed net/400-point absolute textbook limit is zero-sum form of same ceiling. Mahjong/Ace variants remain peripheral.

Unresolved: whether problem intends one-call-per-team textbook 700 gross, two-Grand-per-team 900/1000 club figure, or signed zero-sum net 200. The standard club narrative in round 4 is 700.
